items.title: Fiona the hippo undergoing care after swallowing a hat at Cincinnati Zoo
items.summary: Zookeepers say she cannot have surgery but are providing fluids and supportive care to help her pass the hat.
items.body:
Figure caption,

Watch: Fiona the hippo under observation after eating hat

ByMadeline Halpert

The Cincinnati Zoo in Ohio says its beloved hippopotamus Fiona is undergoing emergency medical care after swallowing a knit hat that slipped into her enclosure.

The Zoo said that Fiona had swallowed the hat about nine days ago and was asymptomatic at first, adding that she was "large enough that a small-ish hat should be passing through".

But a few days later, her appetite started to decrease, and the zoo staff were trying to encourage Fiona to eat to help push the hat through her digestive system.

Fiona rose to fame when she was born premature at the Cincinnati Zoo and at first struggled to survive. Her story inspired an ice cream flavour as well as a character in Cincinnati's ballet.

Michelle Curley, a spokesperson for the zoo, told US media that the hat got into Fiona's enclosure by accident, after a visitor tossed it in the air and it caught on a ceiling fan that flung it through a small opening.

"We probably couldn't make [it] happen again if we tried," Curley said.

Zoo staff have been providing a series of supportive measures like fluids and ultrasounds to help Fiona recover.

The latest ultrasound showed the hat passing through Fiona's small intestine, the staff said, adding that she is still a bit dehydrated.

"Surgery isn't an option for full-grown hippos and our best chance for success with Fiona would be if she could pass this on her own," one of the zookeepers said in an update.

Fiona was born six weeks early to 17-year-old hippo Bibi on 24 January.

At birth she weighed 13 kg (29 lbs), which the zoo said was about half the previous lowest recorded birth weight for her species.

The zoo said staff were "rooting for her and hoping that she proves to be as strong and resilient as she was at the beginning of her life".

translation.title: 辛辛那提动物园河马 Fiona 吞下帽子后正在接受护理
translation.summary: 饲养员说她不能做手术，但正在输液并给予支持性护理，帮助她排出帽子。
translation.label: 机器翻译

blocks.text: 图表说明，
观看：河马 Fiona 在误食帽子后接受观察
作者：Madeline Halpert
俄亥俄州辛辛那提动物园表示，深受喜爱的河马菲奥娜吞下了掉进围栏的一顶针织帽，正在接受紧急医疗救治。
动物园表示，Fiona 大约九天前吞下了那顶帽子，起初没有症状，并称她“体型够大，一顶比较小的帽子应当能通过”。
但几天后，她的食欲开始下降，动物园工作人员试图鼓励菲奥娜进食，以帮助那顶帽子通过消化系统。
Fiona 因在辛辛那提动物园早产出生、起初挣扎求生而走红。她的故事启发了一款冰淇淋口味，以及辛辛那提芭蕾舞剧中的一个角色。
动物园发言人 Michelle Curley 对美国媒体表示，帽子是意外进入 Fiona 的围栏的：一名游客把它抛向空中，帽子挂上了吊扇，被甩进一个小开口。
“我们就算再试，大概也没法再做成[这件事]了，”Curley 说。
动物园工作人员一直在提供输液和超声波等一系列支持措施，帮助菲奥娜康复。
工作人员说，最新超声显示那顶帽子正在通过菲奥娜的小肠，并称她仍有些脱水。
“手术对成年河马来说不是选项，菲奥娜最好的成功机会是她能自己把这个排出来，”一位动物园管理员在更新中说。
Fiona 于 1月24日提早六周出生，母亲是 17 岁的河马 Bibi。
她出生时体重为 13 公斤（29 磅），动物园称这大约只有该物种此前最低出生记录的一半。
动物园表示，工作人员「为她加油，希望她能像生命最初时那样坚强而有韧性」。

items.title: Parents jailed for torture and death of four-year-old girl found along French motorway in 1987
items.summary: Inass Touloub's body was found along the A10 road in 1987, bearing marks of abuse, and was not identified until 2018.
items.body:
Image source, Getty Images

ByKatie Williams

The mother of a four-year-old girl killed in central France and found along a motorway almost 40 years ago has been sentenced to 20 years in prison.

Halima El Bakhti, 72, was found guilty on Tuesday of "torture and acts of barbarity resulting in death without the intent to kill", French media reports.

The girl's father, 74-year-old Ahmed Touloub, was handed a 15-year sentence as an accomplice.

Four-year-old Inass Touloub was found along the A10 road in Suèvres in the Loir-et-Cher department on 11 August 1987. Her body bore multiple marks of abuse, including human bite marks, broken bones and burns with an iron.

She was buried in an unmarked grave near the location where her body was found. Unidentified for three decades, she was known only as the "Little Martyr of the A10".

Then, in 2018, she was identified after the DNA of her brother – tested in an unrelated case – matched with hers, leading to the arrest of their parents.

The trial took place in Loir-et-Cher Assize Court from 2 November, with the verdict delivered on Tuesday after several hours of deliberation.

During the trial, prosecutor Anaïs Allio emphasised that "not a single part of Inass's body was spared", and recalled the "sense of vertigo that overcame us all" upon viewing the "unbearable photographs" from the autopsy, France Info reports.

The jury concluded that the child's mother was suffering from impaired judgement at the time of the girl's death, which reduced the maximum potential sentence.

French media outlet France Info described the two defendants as sitting stoically in chairs before the court with their heads bowed as the reasoning behind the verdict was read out.

El Bakhti and Touloub have 10 days to appeal the verdict.

Inass's death sparked one of France's biggest ever investigations, with the girl's photograph posted in public places and an alert sent to more than 30 countries.

Image source, Getty Images

translation.title: 父母因虐待并导致 1987 年在法国高速公路旁发现的四岁女孩死亡而入狱
translation.label: 机器翻译

blocks.alt: Court sketch shows the parents of Inass Touloub, Halima El Bakhti and Ahmed Touloub, during their trial

blocks.text: 图片来源：Getty Images
作者：Katie Williams
近40年前在法国中部遇害、后在高速公路沿线被发现的一名四岁女孩的母亲，被判处20年监禁。
法国媒体报道，72岁的 Halima El Bakhti 周二被判“酷刑及导致死亡但无杀害故意的野蛮行为”罪名成立。
女孩的父亲、74 岁的 Ahmed Touloub 作为从犯被判 15 年。
1987 年 8 月 11 日，四岁的 Inass Touloub 在卢瓦尔-谢尔省苏埃夫尔的 A10 公路旁被发现。她身上有多处受虐痕迹，包括人的咬痕、骨折以及熨斗烫伤。
她被埋在发现尸体地点附近的一座无名墓中。三十年来身份不明，她只被称为“A10公路的小殉难者”。
随后在2018年，她哥哥在另一起无关案件中接受检测的 DNA 与她的匹配，从而确认了她的身份，并导致父母被捕。
审判自11月2日起在卢瓦-谢尔省巡回法院进行，陪审团经过数小时商议后于周二作出裁决。
France Info 报道，庭审中检察官 Anaïs Allio 强调「Inass 身上没有一处幸免」，并回顾在看到尸检「令人难以忍受的照片」时「我们所有人感受到的眩晕」。
陪审团认定，女孩死亡时其母亲判断力受损，这降低了可能的最高刑期。
法国媒体 France Info 描述称，两名被告在法庭上低头坐在椅子上，神情木然，聆听判决理由的宣读。
El Bakhti 和 Touloub 有 10 天时间对判决提出上诉。
伊纳斯的死亡引发了法国有史以来规模最大的调查之一，女孩的照片被张贴在公共场所，警报被发往30多个国家。

items.title: Israel delays building contracts for West Bank settlement after UK sanctions
items.summary: Attorney general says E1 settlement decision should not be taken by caretaker government led by Netanyahu Israel has postponed issuing contracts for the construction of a large settlement on the West Bank seen as likely to render a two-state solution unviable, days after the UK imposed sanctions aga…
items.body:
Palestinian Bedouin boys play football in Jabal al-Baba, near Ma’aleh Adumim, in the area marked for the E1 settlement. Photograph: Ammar Awad/Reuters

Palestinian Bedouin boys play football in Jabal al-Baba, near Ma’aleh Adumim, in the area marked for the E1 settlement. Photograph: Ammar Awad/Reuters

Israel delays building contracts for West Bank settlement after UK sanctions

Attorney general says E1 settlement decision should not be taken by caretaker government led by Netanyahu

Israel has postponed issuing contracts for the construction of a large settlement on the West Bank seen as likely to render a two-state solution unviable, days after the UK imposed sanctions against building firms operating in the area.

Israeli diplomats insisted the move was not in response to the measures from Downing Street. Gali Baharav-Miara, the attorney general, said any decision on settlement expansion should not be taken by the caretaker government led by Benjamin Netanyahu but by whatever new administration was formed.

She ordered the Israel land authority and ministry of housing not to open the tender process. Israeli diplomats suggested the UK foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, had acted prematurely on Monday in sanctioning the eight construction firms. But UK diplomats believe the growing political pressure on Israel over settlements, including from US Democrats, is having an impact.

Israeli policemen stand guard near the settlement of Ma’aleh Adumim, a West Bank settlement city of nearly 40,000 residents. Photograph: Menahem Kahana/AFP/Getty Images

The deferral puts the E1 settlement expansion in the mix for any coalition negotiations. The leader of the Change bloc, Gadi Eisenkot, seen as Israel’s most likely next prime minister, has been clear in opposing violent settler activity, as has the newly elected Knesset speaker, Matan Kahana, an ally of Eisenkot.

Eisenkot has also opposed the E1 settlement expansion, describing it as a mistake likely to alienate international opinion. He said of the plan: “I recall that Netanyahu himself opposed this for a long time, and due to coalition pressure, he gave in and approved it.”

The EI settlement expansion, due to have been announced on Thursday, has long been seen as qualitatively different since the land – between Jerusalem and Ma’aleh Adumim, a West Bank settlement city of nearly 40,000 residents – bisects the West Bank and cuts it off from East Jerusalem.

Miliband has said it would mark the death knell of a future Palestinian state. The UK, along with a group of European countries, has recently recognised Palestine, and the preservation of a two-state solution has been described as the north star of Labour policy towards the region.

The construction tender was published for more than 3,401 housing units in the area. At the beginning of November, the Israel Defense Forces began demolishing homes in a Bedouin community within the E1 area.

A Palestinian Bedouin walks up a hill in Jabal al-Baba, where development of the planned E1 settlement will displace several Bedouin communities. Photograph: Ammar Awad/Reuters

Israel has already enforced the downgrading of the UK consulate in East Jerusalem as a reprisal for Miliband’s decision in September to try to end trade links with the illegal settlements.

Bennett said: “The British Labour government’s hostility, bias and one-sided approach are particularly glaring given its failure to take any action against the Palestinian Authority, which continues to encourage terrorism through financial payments, promote incitement in its education system and engage in illegal construction in violation of signed agreements.”

Although the Israeli election was largely fought on domestic security-related issues, Eisenkot seems to be more sensitive to the implications of Israel’s crumbling global reputation, and the need to make efforts to be seen to be listening to the criticism. If he becomes prime minister, Eisenkot will, indirectly at least, also have to take account of the views of the Arab parties even if these parties are not going to become members of the government.

The group Peace Now welcomed the attorney general’s decision: “A government that lost the elections is not permitted to exploit its final days in power to advance destructive moves that will endanger Israel’s future and its international standing. Construction in E1 is liable to eliminate the possibility of a two-state solution and drag Israel into a severe diplomatic crisis and international sanctions. The AG’s decision is an important step, but the struggle is not over yet.”

translation.label: 机器翻译

blocks.text: 巴勒斯坦贝都因男孩在靠近马阿莱阿杜明、划为 E1 定居点的 Jabal al-Baba 踢足球。照片：Ammar Awad/Reuters
巴勒斯坦贝都因男孩在靠近马阿莱阿杜明、划为 E1 定居点的 Jabal al-Baba 踢足球。照片：Ammar Awad/Reuters
在英国制裁后，以色列推迟了约旦河西岸定居点的建筑合同
司法部长表示，E1 定居点决定不应由内塔尼亚胡领导的看守政府作出
在英国对在该地区运营的建筑公司实施制裁数日后，以色列推迟签发在约旦河西岸建造一个大型定居点的合同；该定居点被认为很可能使两国方案无法实现。
以色列外交官坚称，此举并非对唐宁街措施的回应。总检察长加利·巴哈拉夫-米亚拉表示，任何扩大定居点的决定都不应由本雅明·内塔尼亚胡领导的看守政府作出，而应由随后组建的新政府决定。
她下令以色列土地管理局和住房部不得启动招标程序。以色列外交官暗示，英国外交大臣 Ed Miliband 周一制裁这八家建筑公司的做法操之过急。但英国外交官认为，包括美国民主党人在内、围绕定居点对以色列施加的不断增大的政治压力正在产生影响。

blocks.alt: Israeli policemen stand near an Israeli flag overlooking Ma’aleh Adumim settlement in the West Bank

blocks.text: 以色列警察在马阿莱阿杜明定居点附近警戒，这是约旦河西岸一座有近4万居民的定居点城市。照片：Menahem Kahana/AFP/Getty Images
这一推迟使 E1 定居点扩建进入任何联合政府谈判的议题之中。被视为以色列最有可能的下任总理的变革集团领导人 Gadi Eisenkot 明确反对定居者暴力活动，新当选的议会主席、Eisenkot 的盟友 Matan Kahana 同样如此。
Eisenkot 也反对 E1 定居点扩建，称之为可能疏远国际舆论的错误。他谈到该计划时说：「我记得内塔尼亚胡本人长期反对此事，后来因为联盟压力才让步并批准了。」
原定于周四宣布的 EI 定居点扩建计划，长期以来一直被视为性质不同，因为这块位于耶路撒冷与马阿莱阿杜明（一座近 4 万居民的约旦河西岸定居点城市）之间的土地，会将约旦河西岸一分为二，并使其与东耶路撒冷隔开。
米利班德曾表示，这将敲响未来巴勒斯坦国的丧钟。英国连同一批欧洲国家最近已承认巴勒斯坦，维护两国方案一直被形容为工党对该地区政策的北极星。
该地区3,401套以上住房的建设招标已经公布。11月初，以色列国防军开始拆除 E1 区域内一个贝都因社区的房屋。

blocks.alt: A Palestinian Bedouin walks up a hill in Jabal al-Baba.

作为对 Miliband 9月决定试图切断与非法定居点贸易往来的报复，以色列已经强制降级了英国在东耶路撒冷的领事馆。

Bennett 说：“英国工党政府的敌意、偏见和一面之词尤其刺眼，因为它未能对巴勒斯坦权力机构采取任何行动。后者仍通过金钱支付鼓励恐怖主义，在教育体系中宣扬煽动，并违反已签署的协议进行非法建设。”
尽管以色列大选主要围绕国内安全相关议题展开，Eisenkot 似乎对以色列全球声誉日益受损的影响、以及需要努力让外界看到自己在倾听批评，更为敏感。如果他成为总理，Eisenkot 至少间接也必须顾及阿拉伯政党的意见，即使这些政党不会成为政府成员。
Peace Now 对总检察长的决定表示欢迎：「一个在选举中落败的政府，不得利用掌权的最后几天推进将危及以色列未来及其国际地位的破坏性举措。在 E1 地区建设，可能消灭两国方案的可能性，并将以色列拖入严重的外交危机和国际制裁。总检察长的决定是重要的一步，但斗争尚未结束。」

items.title: Kuwait says it repelled first Iranian attack in two months after US strikes island
items.summary: Bahrain says it was also attacked by Iran following a US air strike on the Iranian island of Qeshm in the Gulf on Tuesday.
items.body:
Image source, Getty Images

Image caption,

Kuwait condemned the attack, which Iran said targeted an airbase hosting US forces (file photo)

ByDavid Gritten

Kuwait and Bahrain have said they repelled Iranian air attacks overnight as hostilities between Iran and the United States rise.

The drone attack on Kuwait was the first in more than two months. The Iranian army said it had targeted the Ali Al Salem Airbase, which hosts US forces, but Kuwaiti authorities did not report any damage.

It came after US warplanes struck an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, according to US military officials.

Meanwhile, the United Arab Emirates' state oil firm said a crew member was missing after one of its tankers was attacked in the Gulf waterway on Tuesday.

The recent exchanges of fire, as well as deadlock in negotiations on a peace deal, have raised fears of a major escalation in the nine-month-old war.

The conflict began when the US and Israel attacked Iran in late February.

Since then, Iran has retaliated for US and Israeli strikes by launching missiles and drones at Israel and Gulf Arab states hosting US military assets and personnel.

It has also attacked dozens of commercial vessels in and around the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global oil and gas shipments usually pass.

• Pakistani man sentenced to 27 years for Iran-backed plot to kill TrumpPublished13 hours ago

• Trump says US taking 'very seriously' any Iranian plot against WashingtonPublished22 hours ago

• Iran targets US military base in Bahrain with drone attackPublished3 days ago

On Tuesday night, Kuwait's military said its air defences engaged "drone threats" but did not report any casualties or damage.

The Kuwaiti foreign ministry condemned the attack, saying it "flagrantly violated Kuwait's sovereignty, directly threatened its security and stability, and constituted a grave breach of international law".

"The explosions seemed to be coming from far away, but hearing them again after a period of calm was both surprising and worrying," Hani Mohammed, an Egyptian resident of Kuwait, told AFP news agency.

Bahrain's military also said on Wednesday that its air defence systems had "intercepted and destroyed several Iranian aerial attacks".

The island kingdom, which hosts the US Navy's 5th Fleet, has reported four attacks over the past six days, following a two-month lull.

Qatar, which has mediated in the stalled indirect talks between Iran and the US, said the Iranian attacks on its neighbours were a "dangerous escalation that threatens to complicate efforts aimed at containing tensions".

The Iranian army said its drones had targeted US Patriot air defence systems and drone and missile launch platforms at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait.

Later, the army's commander-in-chief, Maj Gen Amir Hatami, warned the US and its allies that it would respond more forcefully to any new attacks on Iran.

"If the enemy repeats its mistake... we have the readiness and the plans to confront it and its supporters in a stronger, more crushing way and without geographic limitations," he said.

On Tuesday night, US fighter jets targeted a missile launch site on Qeshm Island "with precision munitions" in response to Iranian "aggression targeting US personnel and assets", US military officials said.

Iranian media reported explosions on the island but cited a local official as saying they had caused no damage to infrastructure.

In a separate development, the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (Adnoc) said a search-and-rescue operation was under way for a missing sailor following an attack on one of its vessels in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday. The rest of the crew were safely evacuated and 11 were receiving medical care, it added.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) centre reported that a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile about 13 nautical miles (24km) north of Khasab, in Oman's Musandam peninsula. It said the attack caused a fire on board that was extinguished.

Iran said two oil tankers and a ship carrying liquefied natural gas (LNG) had caught fire after hitting naval mines while sailing along an "authorised route".

At least 25 seafarers have been killed across the Middle East since the start of the war, when the Strait of Hormuz was effectively closed due to Iranian missile and drone attacks on commercial vessels and a US naval blockade of Iranian ports.

The US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the conflict and reopen the strait in June, but it collapsed within weeks after Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated its blockade.

Iran insisted it would not give up some measure of control over the waterway and began targeting vessels using a southern route through Omani waters that avoids its preferred route through Iranian waters.

In recent months, the US military has been providing protection for tankers shuttling through the Strait of Hormuz, allowing crude oil exports from Gulf states to reach around 80% of pre-war levels, according to analysts.

科威特谴责了这次袭击；伊朗称袭击目标是一座驻有美军的空军基地（资料照片）
作者：David Gritten
科威特和巴林表示，在伊朗与美国敌对升级之际，它们于夜间击退了伊朗的空袭。
对科威特的无人机袭击是两个多月来的首次。伊朗军方称其目标是驻有美军的阿里·萨利姆空军基地，但科威特当局并未报告任何损坏。
美国军方官员称，此事发生在美军战机袭击霍尔木兹海峡格什姆岛上一处伊朗导弹发射场之后。
与此同时，阿联酋国家石油公司表示，其一艘油轮周二在海湾航道遇袭后，有一名船员失踪。
近期交火以及和平协议谈判陷入僵局，引发了人们对这场已持续九个月的战争出现重大升级的担忧。
冲突始于 2 月下旬美国和以色列进攻伊朗。
此后，伊朗为报复美国和以色列的打击，向以色列以及存放美国军事资产和人员的海湾阿拉伯国家发射了导弹和无人机。
它还袭击了霍尔木兹海峡及其附近数十艘商船，全球约五分之一的油气运输通常经此通过。

blocks.text: 周二夜间，科威特军方表示其防空系统对“无人机威胁”进行了拦截，但未报告任何人员伤亡或损失。
科威特外交部谴责此次袭击，称其“公然侵犯科威特主权，直接威胁其安全与稳定，并构成对国际法的严重违反”。
居住在科威特的埃及人 Hani Mohammed 对法新社说：“爆炸声听起来像是从很远的地方传来，但在一段时间的平静之后再次听到，既令人惊讶，也令人担忧。”
巴林军方周三还表示，其防空系统已“拦截并摧毁了数次伊朗空中袭击”。
这个驻有美国海军第五舰队的岛国，在经过两个月的平静后，过去六天内报告了四次袭击。
曾在陷入停滞的伊朗与美国间接谈判中担任调解方的卡塔尔表示，伊朗对其邻国的袭击是“危险的升级，可能使旨在遏制紧张局势的努力更加复杂”。
伊朗军方表示，其无人机袭击了科威特 Ali Al Salem 空军基地的美国爱国者防空系统以及无人机和导弹发射平台。
随后，陆军总司令 Amir Hatami 少将警告美国及其盟友，对任何针对伊朗的新袭击，将作出更有力的回应。
“如果敌人重蹈覆辙……我们已做好准备，并制定了计划，将以更强、更具毁灭性的方式，且不受地理限制地对抗它及其支持者，”他说。
美国军方官员称，周二夜间，美军战斗机“以精确弹药”打击了格什姆岛上的一处导弹发射场，以回应伊朗“针对美国人员和资产的侵略”。
伊朗媒体报道岛上发生爆炸，但援引当地官员的话说，爆炸并未对基础设施造成损坏。
另据消息，阿布扎比国家石油公司（Adnoc）表示，在其一艘船只周二于霍尔木兹海峡遇袭后，正对一名失踪水手展开搜救。该公司补充称，其余船员已安全撤离，其中 11 人正在接受治疗。
英国海上贸易行动中心（UKMTO）报告称，一艘油轮在阿曼穆桑达姆半岛哈萨布以北约13海里（24公里）处被不明投射物击中。该中心称袭击导致船上起火，火势随后被扑灭。
伊朗表示，两艘油轮和一艘液化天然气（LNG）运输船在沿“核定航线”航行时触碰水雷后起火。
自战争开始以来，中东地区已有至少 25 名海员丧生；当时由于伊朗对商船的导弹和无人机袭击，以及美国海军对伊朗港口的封锁，霍尔木兹海峡实际上已经关闭。
美国与伊朗在6月达成结束冲突并重新开放海峡的初步协议，但数周后因伊朗恢复袭击航运、美国重新实施封锁而破裂。
伊朗坚持不会放弃对该水道一定程度的控制，并开始袭击那些走阿曼水域南线、以避开其偏好的伊朗水域航线的船只。
近几个月来，美国军方一直在为穿行霍尔木兹海峡的油轮提供保护，分析人士称，这使海湾国家的原油出口恢复到了战前水平的约 80%。

items.title: Bancroft sandpaper claims heap pressure on Cummins
items.summary: Cameron Bancroft claims the whole Australia team knew about the 2018 sandpaper plot in explosive revelations that will heap pressure on current captain Pat Cummins.
items.body:
Image source, Getty Images

Image caption,

Cameron Bancroft and Steve Smith were banned for their part in the sandpaper plot

By

Stephan Shemilt

Cricket Correspondent

Updated 2 hours ago

Cameron Bancroft has claimed the whole Australia team knew about the 2018 sandpaper plot in explosive revelations that will heap pressure on current captain Pat Cummins.

In a detailed testimony, published by the West Australian,, external batter Bancroft - the player caught with the sandpaper during the Test match against South Africa - has given arguably the most complete account of the events in Cape Town eight years ago.

"In 2018 not the entire truth was told," said Bancroft. "I have never been completely honest about what happened."

For the past two weeks, Australian cricket has been embroiled in a debate over the ball-tampering saga following the publication of Usman Khawaja's autobiography.

Khawaja wrote that the whole Australia team knew of the plot, claims supported by David Warner and Chadd Sayers. Cummins described Khawaja's account as "wrong" and "nonsense".

On the day Cricket Australia announced a forum into the sandpaper episode, Bancroft published his account, explaining he was motivated by the news conference given by Cummins.

"The final straw for me to write this account was Australian cricket captain Pat Cummins' press conference," said Bancroft.

"It made me feel angry, betrayed and alone.

"What I saw, experienced and lived with - not only him, but everyone else on that tour in South Africa - is not the public account he gave in his press conference and in the years previously when he has spoken on this time."

Opener Bancroft was given a nine-month ban for his part in the plot.

Steve Smith was stripped of the Australia captaincy and given a year-long ban, the same suspension given to vice-captain Warner. No other players or coaches were punished.

In his more than 4,000-word piece, Bancroft has claimed:

• Sandpaper was first used during the second Test against South Africa – the match before Bancroft was caught

• Bancroft had conversations with the Australia seamers – Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Marsh about whether the ball was "swinging enough"

• Before the third day of the second Test, the entire playing group and staff had "celebrations" about the effect of the sandpaper

• When Bancroft was caught during the third Test, then Australia coach Darren Lehmann told 12th man Peter Handscomb to "get the sandpaper off Bangers now"

• Bancroft found the publication of a joint-statement by the Australia bowlers in 2021 "deeply painful".

Khawaja's autobiography and the subsequent claims made by Warner and seamer Sayers have reopened old wounds related to the sandpaper saga.

Still, those connected have remained true to the accounts they have presented during the intervening eight years.

The most significant denial came from Cummins, who rebuffed Khawaja's account in an extraordinary 68-minute address to the media in Sydney. Lehmann and Starc have also reiterated their denials.

Now, it is the extensive detail provided by Bancroft that could shed a whole new light on the controversy and lead to further questions for Cummins, Lehmann and Cricket Australia.

Cummins is due to lead Australia in the first Test against New Zealand on 9 December.

A statement released on behalf of Cummins said: "Whilst we feel for Cam and everything he's been through there's nothing in the statement that hasn't been answered by Pat in his press conference."

A Cricket Australia statement said: "We respect that Cameron Bancroft has told his story, and we will take time to consider his comments.

"We expect that there will be many dimensions to the events of 2018, which is why we have established the forum for individuals to give their version of events.

"We are finalising the terms of reference and will commence the process as soon as possible."

In his account, Bancroft said: "I have spent eight years speaking about accountability, honesty and the lessons I learned from one of Australian cricket's darkest moments.

"However, in 2018 not the entire truth was told. I have never been completely honest about what happened.

"It was not just the three of us — Steve Smith, David Warner and I — who knew about me using sandpaper on the ball in South Africa. It was the whole team.

"When I was questioned during Cricket Australia's investigation, I did not give a complete and truthful account.

"I withheld important details, including when the use of sandpaper began, how long it went on for, and the involvement and awareness of others.

"I did this to protect Cricket Australia's investigation and not implicate others around me."

Bancroft said his actions were "discussed" and "acknowledged" by the entire playing group at the end of the second day and before the beginning of the third day. He said he was encouraged by Saker, who has since worked as a consultant with England.

The only person within the camp to express unease at the ball-tampering, according to Bancroft, was media manager Kate Hutchison.

"I received wraps and encouragement from members of the playing and coaching staff, especially David Saker," said Bancroft.

"Our media manager, Kate Hutchison, expressed her objection to what was happening.

"I recall her making it clear that she believed it was wrong, that she wanted nothing to do with it, and walking away from the discussion.

"I will never forget that. Somebody had spoken up.

"Somebody had demonstrated that being part of the team did not mean having to accept everything the team was doing. And I ignored it."

Bancroft identifies Saker as the coach Khawaja claimed encouraged him to work harder on the ball during the third Test in Cape Town. The 33-year-old said he took "feedback" from all the bowlers and wicketkeeper Tim Paine, who took over the captaincy when Smith was sacked.

In Cape Town, Bancroft was confronted by the umpires when TV cameras showed him concealing the sandpaper in his trousers. He claimed Lehmann sent a message to him via Handscomb.

"Peter Handscomb ran out at the drinks break after I'd been caught and shoved the sandpaper down my pants," wrote Bancroft.

"He said to me: 'I think it's time I take that off you now.' And Pete was doing his job after Boof [Lehmanm] shouted to him on the walkie talkie "get the sandpaper off Bangers [Bancroft] now".

"If he didn't know he wouldn't have said that. And if it wasn't clear enough before, then it was obvious now."

In 2021, Bancroft was playing county cricket with Durham and gave an interview to The Guardian in which he said the bowlers' involvement in the plot was "self-explantory".

In response, Cummins, Starc, Hazlewood and spinner Nathan Lyon released a joint-statement denying any knowledge that ball-tampering had taken place.

"Reading that statement was deeply painful," said Bancroft.

"I had memories of conversations on the field in Port Elizabeth and Newlands, feedback about the ball and shared celebrations that made the statement difficult for me to digest."

Analysis: Potentially the decisive intervention

For almost two weeks, Australian cricket has been at war with itself over the revelations in Usman Khawaja's autobiography.

But there has been an absence of a smoking gun. Without tangible, new, hard evidence, all that was left was claim and counter-claim.

Naturally, the spotlight fell on Pat Cummins because of his role as a bowler in Cape Town and his elevation to Australia captain in the years since.

His performance last week in front of the media, on live television, was extraordinary. For 68 minutes he took all questions and appeared plausible in his answers.

In being so robust in his denial of Khawaja's account - Cummins called it "nonsense" - the skipper also left himself open to the consequences if it was later revealed he was not telling the truth.

Crucially, it was Cummins' press conference that compelled Cameron Bancroft to speak out.

It must be stressed that Bancroft's account is not the open-and-shut evidence that convicts Cummins or anyone else in the dressing room at Newlands in 2018.

But it is certainly the most complete account we have heard from anyone involved, walking step-by-step through the genesis of the plot, the execution and the fallout. Bancroft has named names: Cummins, the other bowlers, Tim Paine, coach Darren Lehmann and assistant coach David Saker. It is, potentially, the decisive intervention that shifts this whole saga in a new direction.

Whether by accident or design, it came on the day Cricket Australia (CA) announced its forum for evidence into the sandpaper controversy. Before Bancroft's account CA's action felt an unsatisfactory halfway house - not an investigation, with no guarantee outcomes will be published.

What now? Will CA go further? How will those implicated by Bancroft respond? How can Cummins lead Australia in the first Test against New Zealand? Could Steve Smith break a silence he has held since the publication of Khawaja's book?

Throughout the past fortnight, there has been a sense that Australian cricket hoped the sandpaper debate would eventually go away. Cummins even said he never wanted to speak about it again.

Instead of fading, the thirst for the truth grows, now fuelled by Bancroft's extraordinary story.

Bancroft had conversations with the Australia seamers – Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Marsh about whether the ball was "swinging enough"
Before the third day of the second Test, the entire playing group and staff had "celebrations" about the effect of the sandpaper
When Bancroft was caught during the third Test, then Australia coach Darren Lehmann told 12th man Peter Handscomb to "get the sandpaper off Bangers now"
Bancroft found the publication of a joint-statement by the Australia bowlers in 2021 "deeply painful".

blocks.text: Khawaja's autobiography and the subsequent claims made by Warner and seamer Sayers have reopened old wounds related to the sandpaper saga.
Still, those connected have remained true to the accounts they have presented during the intervening eight years.
The most significant denial came from Cummins, who rebuffed Khawaja's account in an extraordinary 68-minute address to the media in Sydney. Lehmann and Starc have also reiterated their denials.
Now, it is the extensive detail provided by Bancroft that could shed a whole new light on the controversy and lead to further questions for Cummins, Lehmann and Cricket Australia.
Cummins is due to lead Australia in the first Test against New Zealand on 9 December.
A statement released on behalf of Cummins said: "Whilst we feel for Cam and everything he's been through there's nothing in the statement that hasn't been answered by Pat in his press conference."
A Cricket Australia statement said: "We respect that Cameron Bancroft has told his story, and we will take time to consider his comments.
"We expect that there will be many dimensions to the events of 2018, which is why we have established the forum for individuals to give their version of events.
"We are finalising the terms of reference and will commence the process as soon as possible."
In his account, Bancroft said: "I have spent eight years speaking about accountability, honesty and the lessons I learned from one of Australian cricket's darkest moments.
"However, in 2018 not the entire truth was told. I have never been completely honest about what happened.
"It was not just the three of us — Steve Smith, David Warner and I — who knew about me using sandpaper on the ball in South Africa. It was the whole team.
"When I was questioned during Cricket Australia's investigation, I did not give a complete and truthful account.
"I withheld important details, including when the use of sandpaper began, how long it went on for, and the involvement and awareness of others.
"I did this to protect Cricket Australia's investigation and not implicate others around me."

Bancroft said his actions were "discussed" and "acknowledged" by the entire playing group at the end of the second day and before the beginning of the third day. He said he was encouraged by Saker, who has since worked as a consultant with England.
The only person within the camp to express unease at the ball-tampering, according to Bancroft, was media manager Kate Hutchison.
"I received wraps and encouragement from members of the playing and coaching staff, especially David Saker," said Bancroft.
"Our media manager, Kate Hutchison, expressed her objection to what was happening.
"I recall her making it clear that she believed it was wrong, that she wanted nothing to do with it, and walking away from the discussion.
"I will never forget that. Somebody had spoken up.
"Somebody had demonstrated that being part of the team did not mean having to accept everything the team was doing. And I ignored it."

Bancroft identifies Saker as the coach Khawaja claimed encouraged him to work harder on the ball during the third Test in Cape Town. The 33-year-old said he took "feedback" from all the bowlers and wicketkeeper Tim Paine, who took over the captaincy when Smith was sacked.
In Cape Town, Bancroft was confronted by the umpires when TV cameras showed him concealing the sandpaper in his trousers. He claimed Lehmann sent a message to him via Handscomb.
"Peter Handscomb ran out at the drinks break after I'd been caught and shoved the sandpaper down my pants," wrote Bancroft.
"He said to me: 'I think it's time I take that off you now.' And Pete was doing his job after Boof [Lehmanm] shouted to him on the walkie talkie "get the sandpaper off Bangers [Bancroft] now".
"If he didn't know he wouldn't have said that. And if it wasn't clear enough before, then it was obvious now."
In 2021, Bancroft was playing county cricket with Durham and gave an interview to The Guardian in which he said the bowlers' involvement in the plot was "self-explantory".
In response, Cummins, Starc, Hazlewood and spinner Nathan Lyon released a joint-statement denying any knowledge that ball-tampering had taken place.
"Reading that statement was deeply painful," said Bancroft.
"I had memories of conversations on the field in Port Elizabeth and Newlands, feedback about the ball and shared celebrations that made the statement difficult for me to digest."
Analysis: Potentially the decisive intervention
For almost two weeks, Australian cricket has been at war with itself over the revelations in Usman Khawaja's autobiography.
But there has been an absence of a smoking gun. Without tangible, new, hard evidence, all that was left was claim and counter-claim.
Naturally, the spotlight fell on Pat Cummins because of his role as a bowler in Cape Town and his elevation to Australia captain in the years since.
His performance last week in front of the media, on live television, was extraordinary. For 68 minutes he took all questions and appeared plausible in his answers.
In being so robust in his denial of Khawaja's account - Cummins called it "nonsense" - the skipper also left himself open to the consequences if it was later revealed he was not telling the truth.
Crucially, it was Cummins' press conference that compelled Cameron Bancroft to speak out.
It must be stressed that Bancroft's account is not the open-and-shut evidence that convicts Cummins or anyone else in the dressing room at Newlands in 2018.

But it is certainly the most complete account we have heard from anyone involved, walking step-by-step through the genesis of the plot, the execution and the fallout. Bancroft has named names: Cummins, the other bowlers, Tim Paine, coach Darren Lehmann and assistant coach David Saker. It is, potentially, the decisive intervention that shifts this whole saga in a new direction.

Whether by accident or design, it came on the day Cricket Australia (CA) announced its forum for evidence into the sandpaper controversy. Before Bancroft's account CA's action felt an unsatisfactory halfway house - not an investigation, with no guarantee outcomes will be published.

What now? Will CA go further? How will those implicated by Bancroft respond? How can Cummins lead Australia in the first Test against New Zealand? Could Steve Smith break a silence he has held since the publication of Khawaja's book?
Throughout the past fortnight, there has been a sense that Australian cricket hoped the sandpaper debate would eventually go away. Cummins even said he never wanted to speak about it again.
Instead of fading, the thirst for the truth grows, now fuelled by Bancroft's extraordinary story.

blocks.text: 图片来源：Getty Images
图片说明，
Cameron Bancroft 和 Steve Smith 因参与砂纸阴谋被禁赛
作者
Stephan Shemilt
板球记者
更新于 2 小时前
卡梅伦·班克罗夫特声称整个澳大利亚队都知晓2018年砂纸事件，这一爆炸性披露将给现任队长帕特·卡明斯带来巨大压力。
在《西澳大利亚人报》发表的一份详细证词中，击球手 Bancroft——也就是在对南非的测试赛中被发现持有砂纸的那名球员——对八年前开普敦事件给出了可以说是最完整的叙述。
「2018 年并没有说出全部真相，」班克罗夫特说。「对于所发生的事情，我从未完全诚实。」
过去两周，随着乌斯曼·哈瓦贾自传的出版，澳大利亚板球界陷入了关于篡改球事件的争论。
哈瓦贾写道，整个澳大利亚队都知道这一密谋，大卫·沃纳和查德·塞耶斯的说法也支持这一点。卡明斯则称哈瓦贾的叙述“是错的”、“是胡说”。
就在澳大利亚板球协会宣布就砂纸事件召开研讨会当天，班克罗夫特发表了他的叙述，解释说他是受卡明斯那场新闻发布会推动才这样做的。
班克罗夫特说：「促使我写下这篇陈述的最后一根稻草，是澳大利亚板球队长帕特·卡明斯的新闻发布会。」
“这让我感到愤怒、被背叛，而且孤独。
「我所看到、经历和共同度过的——不仅是他，还有那次南非巡演中的其他所有人——都与他在新闻发布会上以及此前数年谈论这段时期时给出的公开说法不符。」
开局击球手 Bancroft 因参与该阴谋被禁赛九个月。
史蒂夫·史密斯被剥夺澳大利亚队长职务，并被禁赛一年，副队长沃纳也受到同样处罚。其他球员或教练未被处罚。
在这篇超过 4000 字的文章中，Bancroft 声称：

items: 砂纸最早是在对阵南非的第二场测试赛中使用的——也就是班克罗夫特被抓到的前一场比赛
班克罗夫特曾与澳大利亚快速球手——卡明斯、米切尔·斯塔克、乔什·黑兹尔伍德和米切尔·马什——讨论球是否“足够摆动”
在第二场测试赛第三天开始前，全体球员和工作人员曾为砂纸的效果“庆祝”
当 Bancroft 在第三场测试赛中被抓时，时任澳大利亚教练 Darren Lehmann 告诉第12人 Peter Handscomb，“马上把 Bangers 身上的砂纸拿掉”
班克罗夫特认为，澳大利亚投球手在 2021 年发表联合声明「令人深感痛苦」。

blocks.text: 哈瓦贾的自传，以及随后沃纳和快投手塞耶斯的说法，再次揭开了与砂纸丑闻有关的旧伤。
尽管如此，相关人士在其后八年里仍坚持他们此前给出的说法。
最重要的否认来自 Cummins，他在悉尼一场长达 68 分钟的非同寻常的媒体讲话中驳回了 Khawaja 的说法。Lehmann 和 Starc 也再次重申了否认。
如今，Bancroft 提供的大量细节可能为这场争议带来全新视角，并给 Cummins、Lehmann 和 Cricket Australia 带来更多追问。
Cummins 将于 12 月 9 日率澳大利亚队出战对新西兰的首场测试赛。
以 Cummins 名义发布的一份声明说：“虽然我们为 Cam 以及他所经历的一切感到难过，但这份声明里没有什么是 Pat 没有在记者会上回答过的。”
澳大利亚板球协会在声明中说：「我们尊重卡梅伦·班克罗夫特讲述自己的经历，我们将花时间考虑他的言论。
“我们预计2018年事件会有许多层面，这正是我们设立这个论坛、让相关人士陈述各自说法的原因。
「我们正在敲定职权范围，并将尽快启动这一程序。」
在他的叙述中，班克罗夫特说：“八年来，我一直在谈论责任、诚实，以及我从澳大利亚板球最黑暗时刻之一中吸取的教训。
「然而，2018 年并没有说出全部真相。对于所发生的事情，我从未完全诚实。
“不只是我们三个——Steve Smith、David Warner 和我——知道我在南非用砂纸打磨球。而是整个团队都知道。
「在澳大利亚板球协会调查期间接受询问时，我没有提供完整而真实的陈述。
「我隐瞒了重要细节，包括使用砂纸始于何时、持续了多久，以及其他人的参与和知情情况。
「我这样做是为了保护 Cricket Australia 的调查，也不牵连我周围的人。」
班克罗夫特说，他的行为在第二天结束时和第三天开始前“讨论过”并得到全体球员“知晓”。他说自己受到了后来曾担任英格兰队顾问的塞克的鼓励。
据 Bancroft 说，队中唯一对改球行为表示不安的人，是媒体经理 Kate Hutchison。
班克罗夫特说：「我得到了球员和教练组成员的支持和鼓励，尤其是戴维·萨克。」
“我们的媒体经理 Kate Hutchison 对当时正在发生的事表达了反对。
「我记得她明确表示认为那样做是错的，她不想与此事有任何牵连，并离开了讨论。
“我永远不会忘记那件事。有人站出来发声了。
“已经有人表明，作为团队的一员，并不意味着必须接受团队所做的一切。而我当时忽视了这一点。”
Bancroft 指认 Saker 就是 Khawaja 所称、在开普敦第三场测试赛期间鼓励他在球上做更多手脚的教练。这名 33 岁球员说，他听取了所有投球手以及在 Smith 被解职后接任队长的守门员 Tim Paine 的「反馈」。
在开普敦，当电视镜头拍到 Bancroft 把砂纸藏在裤子里时，他被裁判叫住对质。他声称 Lehmann 通过 Handscomb 向他传了话。
“我被抓出局后，Peter Handscomb 在喝水休息时跑出来，把砂纸塞进了我的裤子里，”Bancroft 写道。
“他对我说：‘我觉得现在该把那个从你这儿拿走了。’然后 Pete 在做他的工作，因为 Boof [Lehmanm] 用对讲机朝他喊‘现在把砂纸从 Bangers [Bancroft] 那儿拿下来’。”
「如果他不知道，就不会那样说。如果之前还不够清楚，那现在已经显而易见了。」
2021 年，班克罗夫特当时在达勒姆打郡级板球，并接受《卫报》采访，称投球手参与这一密谋是“不言自明的”。
对此，Cummins、Starc、Hazlewood 以及旋转球投手 Nathan Lyon 发表联合声明，否认知晓发生过改球行为。
“读到那份声明让人深感痛苦，”Bancroft 说。
“我记得在伊丽莎白港和新地的场上交谈、关于球的反馈，以及一起庆祝的场面，这些都让那份声明让我难以接受。”
分析：这可能是决定性的干预
近两周来，澳大利亚板球界因 Usman Khawaja 自传中的爆料而陷入内斗。
但一直缺少决定性证据。没有切实、新的硬证据，剩下的就只是指控与反驳。
自然地，焦点落在了 Pat Cummins 身上，因为他曾在开普敦担任投手，此后又升任澳大利亚队长。
他上周在媒体面前、在电视直播中的表现非同寻常。在68分钟里，他回答了所有问题，而且答得看似可信。
Cummins 对 Khawaja 的说法否认得如此强硬——他称之为“一派胡言”——也让自己面临风险：如果后来被发现他没有讲真话，将承担相应后果。
关键的是，正是 Cummins 的新闻发布会迫使 Cameron Bancroft 站出来发声。
必须强调的是，Bancroft 的说法并不是可以据此认定 Cummins 或2018年纽兰兹更衣室里其他任何人有罪的铁证。
但这无疑是我们从任何当事人那里听到的最完整叙述，一步步梳理了密谋的缘起、实施和后果。班克罗夫特点出了名字：Cummins、其他投手、Tim Paine、教练 Darren Lehmann 和助理教练 David Saker。这有可能成为把整场风波推向新方向的决定性介入。
无论是巧合还是有意安排，此事发生在澳大利亚板球协会（CA）宣布就砂纸争议举行证据听证会的同一天。在班克罗夫特作出说明之前，CA 的举动显得像一个不能令人满意的折中方案——不是调查，也不能保证结果会公布。
接下来呢？CA 还会再进一步吗？被 Bancroft 点名的人会如何回应？Cummins 如何带领澳大利亚出战对新西兰的第一场测试赛？Steve Smith 会不会打破自 Khawaja 的书出版以来一直保持的沉默？
在过去两周里，人们有一种感觉：澳大利亚板球界希望砂纸争议最终会自行平息。Cummins 甚至说过，他再也不想谈论这件事。
对真相的渴望不减反增，如今更因 Bancroft 的非凡故事而愈发强烈。

items.title: Democrats win Alaska Senate race two weeks after midterms counting began
items.summary: Confirmation of Mary Peltola's victory caps of the party's rout of the Republicans in the midterms Senate election.
items.body:
Image source, Bloomberg via Getty Images

Image caption,

Mary Peltola defeated the state's Republican incumbent after a controversial race

ByKayla Epstein, National reporter and Shaimaa Khalil, North America correspondent

Updated 2 hours ago

Democrat Mary Peltola has won Alaska's hard-fought Senate race, completing a sweeping victory for the party in the US upper house in the midterm elections.

The win gives the Democrats a 56th Senate seat following a tumultuous and controversial election in Alaska, which featured alleged spoiler recruitment efforts and unprecedented court battles.

It took two full weeks of counting to call a winner in the 3 November poll due to the logistical challenge of collecting ballots from across the state's remote expanse.

It is the ninth Senate seat the Democrats have taken from Republicans in the midterms, giving the party control of the US Congress for the last two years of Donald Trump's presidency.

The Democrats also won back the House of Representatives, the lower chamber.

Peltola defeated the incumbent Republican senator, Dan S Sullivan, who is yet to comment.

In her victory statement, Peltola said the "status quo in DC is not working for Alaska".

She recalled speaking to "elders in tears about empty fish racks" and to parents in rural Alaska choosing between heating their homes and putting food on the table.

Peltola is the first Alaska Native elected to the US Senate, and is the first Democrat to win a US Senate seat in Alaska since 2008.

Donald Trump won the state by 13 points in the 2024 presidential election, but defeat for the Republicans in this year's US Senate race in the state caps off a string of losses in the midterms for the president's party.

Many voters across the United States cited cost-of-living issues as a factor that affected how they cast their ballots.

• Trump says Alaska voters chose the wrong Dan Sullivan. What does the data show?Published4 hours ago

• Could Alaska's fishing industry tilt Washington's balance of power?Published3 November

Peltola's campaign had come under fire after the New York Times, external reported that her team worked with people who tried to recruit so-called spoiler candidates in an alleged attempt to confuse voters.

The alleged scheme led to a candidate named Daniel J Sullivan - a complete political unknown residing in a small coastal town who shared a name with the state's current US Senator and incumbent, Dan S Sullivan - contesting the race.

After legal challenges, state courts ruled that Daniel J Sullivan could remain on the ballot, and election officials distinguished them on election materials.

Peltola denied having knowledge of the alleged plot but her campaign swiftly came under fire, and both the US justice department and Alaska's Republican governor said they would launch investigations.

The Trump administration also filed a lawsuit attempting to stop the certification of the election results if the incumbent Republican Senator Sullivan lost.

A federal judge, though, dismissed the case, following legal challenges from Alaska election officials as well as the Peltola campaign and voting groups.

Due to Alaska's ranked-choice voting system, voters confused about which Dan Sullivan was the incumbent could have simply chosen both men, listing them as their first and second choices.

If they did so, after the first round of voting was complete, tabulation would have re-allocated any votes from Daniel J Sullivan - who stood little to no chance of winning - to Dan S Sullivan.

Experts told the BBC that this process made it difficult for any potential spoiler candidate to have any impact on the results.

An analysis by BBC Verify found that even if every vote for Daniel J Sullivan had gone to the incumbent, Dan S Sullivan, Peltola would still have won.

The Democratic win in Alaska cements the party's majority in the US Senate, as the party now has 56 seats to the Republicans' 44.

The most senior Democrat in the Senate, Chuck Schumer, said Peltola had run "a pitch-perfect campaign devoted to the issues Alaskans care most about". Hailing the Democrats' final tally in the Senate, he said: "56 seats was an unimaginable result even just a few months ago."

The Alaska seat was initially one of several toss-up races that appeared as a must-win for Democrats if they wanted to gain control of the US Senate. But by the time Peltola was called the winner, they had seats to spare.

With 99% of ballots counted, Peltola had slightly more than 50% of the votes, while Sullivan trailed on less than 46%.

Sullivan, a former Alaska attorney general and an ally of Trump, campaigned on his record of delivering energy and military investment for the state.

Peltola promised Alaskans a more independent voice in Washington.

"As a lifelong Alaskan who has dedicated my life to serving our state, there is no greater honor than having Alaskans' support in our fight to take on corporate greed, lower costs, and put Alaska first," she said in her victory statement.

"I will stand up to anyone to take on the rigged system in DC and deliver results for Alaska's working families."

translation.label: 机器翻译

blocks.text: 图片来源，Bloomberg via Getty Images
图片说明，
Mary Peltola 在一场有争议的选举中击败了该州的共和党现任者
作者：全国记者 Kayla Epstein 与北美记者 Shaimaa Khalil
更新于 2 小时前
民主党人 Mary Peltola 赢得了竞争激烈的阿拉斯加州参议院选举，完成该党在中期选举中对美国参议院的压倒性胜利。
这场胜利使民主党在参议院获得第 56 个席位，此前阿拉斯加经历了一场动荡且充满争议的选举，其中包括涉嫌招募“搅局者”以及前所未有的法庭交锋。
由于需要从该州偏远广袤的各地收集选票，后勤困难重重，11月3日的选举花了整整两周才清点出获胜者。
这是民主党在中期选举中从共和党手中拿下的第九个参议院席位，使该党在 Donald Trump 总统任期的最后两年掌控美国国会。
民主党还赢回了众议院，即议会下院。
Peltola 击败了现任共和党参议员 Dan S Sullivan，后者尚未置评。
Peltola 在胜选声明中表示，「华盛顿的现状并不适合阿拉斯加」。
她回忆说，曾与“对着空鱼架落泪的长者”交谈，也和阿拉斯加农村的父母谈过，他们要在取暖和吃饭之间做选择。
Peltola 是首位当选美国参议员的阿拉斯加原住民，也是自 2008 年以来首位在阿拉斯加赢得参议院席位的民主党人。
唐纳德·特朗普在 2024 年总统选举中以 13 个百分点赢得该州，但共和党在今年该州美国参议院竞选中的失利，为总统所属政党在中期选举中的一连串失败画上了句号。
美国各地许多选民将生活成本问题列为影响投票决定的因素。

items: 特朗普称阿拉斯加选民选错了 Dan Sullivan。数据怎么说？发表于4小时前
阿拉斯加渔业会否改变华盛顿的权力平衡？发表于11月3日

blocks.text: 佩尔托拉的竞选团队在《纽约时报》报道称其团队与试图招募所谓“搅局候选人”的人员合作、据称意在迷惑选民后，受到抨击。
据称，这一计划导致一名叫 Daniel J Sullivan 的候选人参选——他是完全不为人知的政治素人，住在一座沿海小镇，却与该州现任联邦参议员、寻求连任的 Dan S Sullivan 同名。
在经历法律挑战后，州法院裁定丹尼尔·J·沙利文可以继续留在选票上，选举官员也在选举材料中对两人作了区分。
Peltola 否认知晓所谓密谋，但她的竞选很快遭到抨击，美国司法部和阿拉斯加的共和党州长均表示将展开调查。
特朗普政府还提起诉讼，试图在现任共和党参议员沙利文落选时阻止选举结果认证。
不过，在阿拉斯加选举官员以及 Peltola 竞选团队和投票团体提出法律质疑后，一名联邦法官驳回了该案。
由于阿拉斯加的排序选择投票制度，搞不清哪位 Dan Sullivan 才是现任者的选民本可以两人一起选，把他们分别列为第一和第二选择。
如果他们这样做，在第一轮投票结束后，计票会把 Daniel J Sullivan——几乎没有胜算的那一位——的选票重新分配给 Dan S Sullivan。
专家对英国广播公司表示，这一程序让任何潜在的搅局候选人很难对结果产生影响。
BBC Verify 的分析发现，即使投给 Daniel J Sullivan 的每一票都给了现任者 Dan S Sullivan，Peltola 仍然会获胜。

blocks.alt: A bar chart showing each candidate's share of first-choice votes: Mary Peltola (Dem): 50.1%, Dan S Sullivan (Rep): 45.8%, Gerald L Heikes (Rep): 2.1%, Daniel J Sullivan Jr: 1.7%, Write-in: 0.3%. After 99% of the votes counted

blocks.text: 民主党在阿拉斯加的胜利巩固了该党在美国参议院的多数地位，目前民主党拥有 56 席，共和党 44 席。
参议院最高级别的民主党人查克·舒默表示，佩尔托拉开展了“一场完美的竞选，专注于阿拉斯加人最关心的问题”。在称赞民主党在参议院的最终席位数时，他说：“56 个席位即便在几个月前也是难以想象的结果。”
阿拉斯加这个席位最初是几场摇摆选情之一，民主党若想拿下参议院控制权，似乎必须拿下它。但等 Peltola 被宣布获胜时，他们已经有了多余的席位。
在 99% 的选票已统计的情况下，佩尔托拉获得略高于 50% 的选票，沙利文落后，得票率不足 46%。
Sullivan 曾担任阿拉斯加州总检察长，是特朗普的盟友，他以推动该州能源和军事投资的政绩展开竞选。
Peltola 向阿拉斯加民众承诺，将在华盛顿发出更独立的声音。
「作为一生奉献于本州的阿拉斯加居民，在抗击企业贪婪、降低成本、把阿拉斯加放在第一位的斗争中得到阿拉斯加人民的支持，是最大的荣誉，」她在胜选声明中说。
「我将对抗任何人，挑战华盛顿那套被操纵的体制，为阿拉斯加的工薪家庭交出成果。」

items.body:
Smoke plumes rise on Myanmar’s side of border as Rohingya refugees walk on the shore after crossing the Bangladesh-Myanmar border by boat. Photograph: Danish Siddiqui/Reuters

Smoke plumes rise on Myanmar’s side of border as Rohingya refugees walk on the shore after crossing the Bangladesh-Myanmar border by boat. Photograph: Danish Siddiqui/Reuters

Fears grow that US will impose sanctions on ICJ judges ahead of Myanmar genocide ruling

A ruling against Myanmar could set precedent for court’s judgment on Israel’s actions in Gaza

Fears are growing that the US could impose sanctions on judges at the international court of justice, including this year’s Nobel peace prize winner, Navi Pillay, if the court rules on Thursday that the Myanmar government committed genocide against the Rohingya.

‘They showed no mercy’: mapping the Rohingya villages being erased by rebel forces

Read more

The ICJ has never found a state responsible for committing genocide, and a significant factor in previous cases has been how to prove “intent” in a crime defined as acts committed with the “intent to destroy, in whole or in part” a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.

Lawyers representing Rohingya survivors say patterns of behaviour by Myanmar’s military, including killing people as they fled, show clear attempts to destroy the group during assaults on Rakhine state in 2016 and 2017.

It is the role of independent judges to interpret the genocide convention. However, judges at the court have taken advice on how to protect their assets from potential US sanctions, as a genocide ruling could be interpreted by Washington as lowering the “legal threshold” for the crime.

The Foundation for Defense of Democracies, an influential thinktank close to the White House, has predicted a genocide ruling will lead to the US imposing sanctions on the ICJ.

A man cries during a protest in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, condemning violence against Rohingya people in Rakhine state, Myanmar. Photograph: Fazry Ismail/EPA

The US and Israel fear the final judgment may clarify how to establish a government’s intent to commit a genocide, and so set a precedent that makes it more likely the court will later rule that Israel committed genocide in Gaza.

Myanmar, which has denied carrying out a genocide, claims its actions targeted a military uprising by insurgents.

The ICJ, sometimes described as the UN’s top court, is responsible for settling interstate disputes, unlike the international criminal court (ICC), which prosecutes individuals accused of war crimes and other international crimes.

The US has already imposed crippling sanctions on judges at the ICC after the court issued arrest warrants against the Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu. The US has also announced sanctions against the entire ICC as an institution, which it described as a “rogue court”. Washington fears the ICC could go after US troops.

Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu at a joint news conference in the White House last year. Photograph: Win McNamee/Getty Images

The Gambia, as a litigant, was entitled to appoint an ad hoc judge in the case against Myanmar and chose the South African lawyer Pillay, who in October was awarded the Nobel peace prize. She is required to act as a jurist and not an advocate for the Gambia.

Mike Waltz, the US ambassador to the UN, has sent a warning shot to Pillay and the 15 ICJ judges, saying Washington “will not allow globalist, faux judges to weaponise the law against our troops”.

Waltz asserted last month: “The ICJ ad hoc judge Navi Pillay is tipping the scales on the ICJ’s current proceedings on Myanmar, intending to lower the legal threshold for proving genocide so that weakened and false standard can later be weaponised against American and allied soldiers whenever they raise a finger against terrorists that hide behind civilians.”

In remarks addressed to Pillay, he said: “We see your agenda and we’ll be watching the ICJ’s handling of these proceedings very closely.”

In a speech last Friday, the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, said: “For this global elite, international law … is an instrument to advance their interests under the pretence of universal principles.”

after newsletter promotion

He warned the ICC against quoting laws to “men with swords”.

Israel has previously criticised adverse advisory opinions issued by the ICJ and refused to implement 2024 orders requiring Israel to admit more aid into Gaza, and to cooperate with Unrwa, the UN relief and works agency.

Palestinians search for bodies and survivors among the rubble in a destroyed area after Israeli airstrikes in Gaza City, in October 2023. Photograph: Mohammed Saber/EPA

In the Myanmar case, a 24-page submission jointly filed by the UK and five other mainly European states, argued that the ICJ, in judging intent to commit genocide, should examine a range of “facts and circumstances” assessed “comprehensively and holistically”.

It also stressed that genocide was not solely defined by killings, and that the treatment of children, gender-based violence and forced displacement were also relevant.

The US until recently had taken a relatively more benign view of The Hague-based ICJ, and under Antony Blinken as US secretary of state determined that Myanmar had committed genocide.

The 15 ICJ judges are elected for nine-year terms by the UN security council and the UN general assembly.

Rubio has given the ICC until April to respond to his criticisms before he imposes sanctions.

On Friday, the ICC formally decided to drop plans to prosecute US soldiers and intelligence agents for potentially unlawful acts in Afghanistan. The shelving of the near-dormant inquiry came after it was agreed evidence would be hard to obtain, but one side-effect may be a greater willingness on the part of the US to abandon its plan to impose sanctions on the ICC.

blocks.text: 罗兴亚难民乘船越过孟加拉国与缅甸边境后走在岸边，缅甸一侧升起烟柱。照片：Danish Siddiqui/Reuters
罗兴亚难民乘船越过孟加拉国与缅甸边境后走在岸边，缅甸一侧升起烟柱。照片：Danish Siddiqui/Reuters
缅甸种族灭绝裁决前，外界越来越担心美国将对国际法院法官实施制裁
一项对缅甸不利的裁决，可能为该法院就以色列在加沙的行动作出判决树立先例
人们日益担心，如果国际法院周四裁定缅甸政府对罗兴亚人实施了种族灭绝，美国可能对国际法院的法官实施制裁，其中包括今年的诺贝尔和平奖得主 Navi Pillay。
“他们毫不留情”：绘制正被叛军抹去的罗兴亚村落地图
阅读更多
国际法院（ICJ）从未认定一个国家犯有灭绝种族罪，而以往案件中的一个重要因素是如何证明“意图”——该罪行被定义为以“全部或部分毁灭”某一民族、族裔、种族或宗教群体的“意图”实施的行为。
代表罗兴亚幸存者的律师表示，缅甸军方的行为模式，包括在人们逃离时加以杀害，显示出其在 2016 年和 2017 年袭击若开邦期间企图毁灭该群体的明显意图。
解释《灭绝种族罪公约》是独立法官的职责。不过，该法院的法官已就如何保护其资产免受潜在美国制裁征求建议，因为一项灭绝种族罪裁决可能被华盛顿解读为降低了该罪行的“法律门槛”。
与白宫关系密切的有影响力智库 Foundation for Defense of Democracies 预测，种族灭绝裁决将导致美国对国际法院（ICJ）实施制裁。

blocks.alt: A Rohingya man wearing a “Stop Killings” headband cries during a crowded protest

blocks.text: 一名男子在马来西亚吉隆坡的抗议中哭泣，抗议谴责缅甸若开邦针对罗兴亚人的暴力。照片：Fazry Ismail/EPA
美国和以色列担心，最终判决可能澄清如何认定一个政府实施种族灭绝的意图，从而形成一个先例，使该法院日后更有可能裁定以色列在加沙实施了种族灭绝。
否认实施种族灭绝的缅甸声称，其行动针对的是反叛分子发动的军事暴动。
国际法院（ICJ）有时被称为联合国的最高法院，负责解决国家之间的争端，这与起诉被控战争罪及其他国际罪行个人的国际刑事法院（ICC）不同。
在国际刑事法院对以色列总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡发出逮捕令后，美国已对该法院的法官实施了严厉制裁。美国还宣布对整个国际刑事法院作为机构实施制裁，称之为“流氓法院”。华盛顿担心国际刑事法院可能追查美国士兵。

blocks.alt: Netanyahu gestures while speaking at a podium as Trump stands behind another

blocks.text: 唐纳德·特朗普与本雅明·内塔尼亚胡去年在白宫举行联合新闻发布会。照片：Win McNamee/Getty Images
作为诉讼方，冈比亚有权在对缅甸的案件中任命一名专案法官，并选择了南非律师 Pillay；她在 10 月获得了诺贝尔和平奖。她必须以法学家身份行事，而不能充当冈比亚的辩护人。
美国驻联合国大使 Mike Waltz 向 Pillay 和 15 名国际法院法官发出警告，称华盛顿“不会允许全球主义的、冒牌法官把法律武器化来对付我们的军队”。
Waltz 上个月断言：“国际法院专案法官 Navi Pillay 正在影响国际法院目前关于缅甸的诉讼，意图降低证明种族灭绝的法律门槛，以便日后这个被削弱且不实的标准，可以被用来对付美国及其盟国士兵，只要他们稍微动手对付躲在平民身后的恐怖分子。”
他在对皮莱的讲话中说：「我们看清了你的议程，也将密切关注国际法院对这些程序的处理。」
美国国务卿马尔科·鲁比奥上周五在演讲中说：“对这个全球精英阶层来说，国际法……是他们打着普遍原则的幌子推进自身利益的工具。”
跳过新闻通讯推广
新闻通讯推广之后
他警告 ICC，不要对着“持剑的人”引用法律。
以色列此前曾批评国际法院作出的不利咨询意见，并拒绝执行 2024 年要求以色列允许更多援助进入加沙、以及与联合国近东救济工程处（Unrwa）合作的命令。

blocks.text: 2023年10月以色列空袭加沙城后，巴勒斯坦人在被毁区域的废墟中搜寻尸体和幸存者。照片：Mohammed Saber/EPA
在缅甸案中，英国与另外五个主要以欧洲国家为主的国家共同提交了一份 24 页意见书，主张国际法院在判断种族灭绝意图时，应「全面而整体地」审视一系列「事实与情形」。
它还强调，种族灭绝并非仅由杀戮界定，对儿童的待遇、基于性别的暴力和强迫流离失所也同样相关。
直到不久前，美国对总部位于海牙的国际法院（ICJ）态度相对温和，并在 Antony Blinken 担任国务卿期间认定缅甸实施了种族灭绝。
国际法院的 15 名法官由联合国安理会和联合国大会选举产生，任期九年。
Rubio 已给 ICC 到 4 月的期限，要求其回应他的批评，否则他将实施制裁。

items.title: British hacker who stole $11m through text message scheme jailed for six years in US
items.summary: Tyler Buchanan, from Dundee, was a member of the notorious Scattered Spider group and began hacking when he was a teenager.
items.body:
Image source, Policía Nacional

Image caption,

Spanish police arrested Buchanan in Madrid

ByJoe Tidy

Cyber correspondent, BBC World Service

A British hacker has been sentenced to six years in a federal prison in the US for conspiring to hack into at least a dozen companies via text message phishing, and stealing more than $11.6m (£8.8m) in cryptocurrency from individual victims.

Tyler Buchanan, 24, from Dundee, started hacking as a teenager and was part of the collective of young hackers known as Scattered Spider, which has been blamed for a string of high profile cyber-crimes.

US prosecutors said the thefts had "severe, life-altering consequences" for victims and showed the growing threat posed by online crime groups.

The sentence brings to an end a years-long international investigation involving authorities in the UK, US, Spain and Canada.

Buchanan admitted taking part in a hacking campaign that began in 2021, when he was 19.

Working from his parents' home, he and other English-speaking hackers in the US and UK targeted employees at major technology and telecommunications companies.

It made them $8m in less than two years, according to US prosecutors.

Buchanan and his hacker gang sent out hundreds of SMS messages to the mobile phones of people who worked for large tech or telecoms companies.

The SMS phishing messages contained links to spoof websites designed to look like legitimate sites of victim companies.

The group used messages like "Hi, your account is due to expire - you need to log in to your work account here immediately or you will lose access to work apps".

The websites then lured the recipient into providing confidential information, including personal identifying information (PII), and account usernames and passwords.

The boys and young men did it on an industrial scale with Buchanan setting up a Telegram bot to collect all the victims' credentials as the duped workers unwittingly handed over their login details.

For some victim companies, subsequently stolen information included confidential work information, intellectual property, plus account access credentials, names, email addresses, and telephone numbers.

The group then used stolen information and SIM-swapping techniques to target cryptocurrency investors in the United States.

In the largest single theft, prosecutors said one victim lost $1.67m in December 2022.

Overall, authorities calculated that Buchanan and his co-conspirators stole more than $11.6m from victims.

Threatened with a blowtorch

Buchanan was also a victim of cyber-criminals.

In early 2023 his online identity and home address were leaked by rival hackers seeking access to his cryptocurrency.

Cyber security researchers and journalists reported that he was assaulted at his home and threatened with a blowtorch.

"TylerB and his group were highly sophisticated and organised but the violence he and others experienced was a sign of the troubling direction of these online communities of young hackers" says cyber security researcher Allison Nixon from Unit221B.

Buchanan then reportedly fled to Canada to escape further threats before returning home.

In April 2023, officers from Police Scotland searched Buchanan's bedroom after receiving a request from the FBI.

Investigators recovered a device containing the names and addresses of hacking victims, along with cryptocurrency seed phrases and account credentials belonging to at least one victim.

The following month, Buchanan left the UK again.

He was arrested on 31 May 2024 at Palma de Mallorca Airport in Spain while attempting to board a private flight to Naples.

After being extradited to the United States, he remained in custody before being sentenced this week.

In his November 2023 charge, Buchanan was named along with four American men and boys in their twenties and teens for alleged activity linked to the notorious cyber-criminal collective Scattered Spider.

They have all pleaded guilty too and are now serving time in jail.

Two other members of the Scattered Spider group were jailed in the UK in July for various cyber attacks including a disruptive one against Transport for London that caused £39m of damage.

translation.title: 通过短信骗局盗走 1100 万美元的英国黑客在美国被判六年监禁
translation.label: 机器翻译

blocks.alt: Image of two officers escorting Buchanan into the police station. Buchanan is a tall and large white man with a green t shirt.

blocks.text: 图片来源：Policía Nacional
图片说明，
西班牙警方在马德里逮捕了 Buchanan
作者：Joe Tidy
网络事务记者，BBC 国际台
一名英国黑客因合谋通过短信钓鱼入侵至少十几家公司，并从个人受害者处盗取超过 1,160 万美元（880 万英镑）的加密货币，被判处在美国联邦监狱服刑六年。
来自邓迪、现年24岁的泰勒·布坎南少年时就开始黑客活动，曾是名为 Scattered Spider 的年轻黑客团体的一员，该团体被指应对一系列高调网络犯罪负责。
美国检察官表示，这些盗窃给受害者造成了「严重的、改变人生的后果」，也显示出网络犯罪团伙构成的日益增长的威胁。
这项判决为历时数年、涉及英国、美国、西班牙和加拿大当局的国际调查画上了句号。
Buchanan 承认参与了始于 2021 年的黑客行动，当时他 19 岁。
他在父母家中工作，与美国和英国的其他英语黑客一起，将大型科技和电信公司的员工列为目标。
据美国检方称，他们在不到两年里赚了 800 万美元。
布坎南和他的黑客团伙向大型科技或电信公司员工的手机发送了数百条短信。
这些短信钓鱼信息包含指向伪装成受害公司正规网站的仿冒网站链接。
该团伙使用类似这样的消息：“您好，您的账户即将过期——您需要立即在此处登录工作账户，否则将失去对工作应用的访问权限。”
这些网站随后诱使收件人提供机密信息，包括个人身份信息（PII）以及账户用户名和密码。
这些男孩和年轻男子以工业化的规模实施此事，Buchanan 设立了一个 Telegram 机器人来收集所有受害者的凭证，被骗的员工在毫不知情的情况下交出了登录信息。
对一些受害公司而言，随后被盗的信息包括机密工作信息、知识产权，以及账户访问凭证、姓名、电子邮件地址和电话号码。
该团伙随后利用窃取的信息和 SIM 卡互换手法，将目标对准美国的加密货币投资者。
检方表示，在单笔最大的盗窃案中，一名受害者于 2022 年 12 月损失了 167 万美元。
当局总体估算，布坎南及其同谋从受害者那里窃取了超过 1160 万美元。
被喷灯威胁
Buchanan 也是网络犯罪的受害者。
2023 年初，他的网络身份和家庭住址被试图窃取其加密货币的对手黑客泄露。
网络安全研究人员和记者报道称，他在家中遭到袭击，并被人用喷灯威胁。
“TylerB及其团伙高度老练且组织严密，但他和其他人所遭受的暴力，表明这些年轻黑客在线社区令人不安的走向，”Unit221B的网络安全研究员艾莉森·尼克森说。
据报，Buchanan 随后逃往加拿大以躲避进一步威胁，之后才返回家中。
2023 年 4 月，苏格兰警方在接到联邦调查局的请求后搜查了布坎南的卧室。
调查人员找回了一台设备，其中存有黑客攻击受害者的姓名和地址，以及属于至少一名受害者的加密货币助记词和账户凭证。
次月，Buchanan 再次离开英国。
他于 2024 年 5 月 31 日在西班牙马略卡岛帕尔马机场被捕，当时正试图搭乘一架飞往那不勒斯的私人航班。
被引渡到美国后，他一直被羁押，并于本周被判刑。
在2023年11月的起诉中，布坎南与四名二十多岁及青少年的美国男子一同被点名，涉嫌与臭名昭著的网络犯罪团体 Scattered Spider 有关的活动。
他们也都已认罪，目前正在狱中服刑。
Scattered Spider 组织的另外两名成员今年7月在英国入狱，罪名是多项网络攻击，其中包括一次针对伦敦交通局、造成3900万英镑损失的破坏性攻击。

items.title: Ghana's new $60m presidential jet sparks public outrage
items.summary: The purchase has sparked outrage over its cost as many Ghanaians struggle with rising cost of living.
items.body:
Image source, Ghana Air Force

Image caption,

The French-made Falcon 6X replaces the ageing presidential jet, officials say

ByWycliffe Muia

Updated 3 hours ago

Ghana's government has defended its purchase of a new presidential jet amid criticism over its cost, as many citizens continue to struggle with the high cost of living.

The $60m (£46m) French-made Falcon 6X has sparked a political row, with opposition politicians accusing President John Mahama's administration of misplaced priorities.

But the government says the purchase is justified, arguing that Ghana's improving economy makes the aircraft affordable and is needed to replace an ageing presidential jet.

The controversy comes as Mahama's administration seeks to demonstrate an economic recovery after years of financial difficulties that forced Ghana to seek IMF assistance.

• Can Ghana's new president meet the voters' high expectations?Published7 January 2025

Manufactured by French aerospace company Dassault Aviation, the aircraft was delivered to the Ghana Air Force on Monday at a reported cost of $61m.

Parliament approved its purchase last December as part of a broader programme to modernise Ghana's military aviation fleet, which also includes four helicopters from Airbus.

The jet was welcomed with a water salute on Monday, but its arrival triggered criticism online and among opposition politicians over the cost and timing of the purchase.

While in the opposition, Mahama himself opposed buying a new presidential jet, prompting questions about why his administration has now gone head with the purchase.

Opposition MP Samuel Abu Jinapor questioned the government's priorities, saying the expenditure came at a time when many Ghanaians continue to struggle with the cost of living and youth unemployment remained alarmingly high.

"What was unacceptable in opposition cannot suddenly become acceptable in government merely because the occupants of power have changed," Jinapor added.

He accused the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) of hypocrisy, recalling how its senior figures had strongly opposed proposals for a new presidential aircraft when they were in opposition.

Jinapor also called for greater transparency over the procurement process, how the purchase was financed and the government's justification for the expenditure.

Image source, Ghana Air Force

Image caption,

Defence Minister Kenneth Adjei welcomed and inspected the new jet on Monday

The purchase has also prompted sharp criticism on social media, with some users arguing the money could have been spent on more pressing public needs.

"This money can employ over 100,000 nurses and 200,000 teachers," an X user posted.

But the government has rejected the criticism, saying Ghana's economic circumstances have changed considerably since the NDC opposed a similar purchase.

Peter Lanchene Toobu, chairman of parliament's defence committee, said the party had never opposed acquiring a presidential jet in principle.

Its objection, he said, had been on the timing when Ghana was experiencing severe economic difficulties.

"We agreed in principle that we needed to purchase a new presidential jet," he said.

He argued, however, that Ghana could not justify the expenditure at a time when it was seeking a $3bn bailout from the IMF.

"The strength and macroeconomic stability of this country have enhanced our status in the sense that imports have become cheaper, and this is the right time," he added.

Toobu said the government had purchased the aircraft without borrowing, citing a stronger Ghanaian currency and improved economic conditions.

Government spokesperson Kwakye Ofosu also dismissed suggestions that the purchase was a misplaced priority.

He pointed to falling prices of construction materials and lower borrowing costs as evidence of the country's improved economic situation.

"When I was campaigning in 2024, and I was donating cement, it cost 115 cedis (£7.5) a bag. Today, for 80 cedis, you will get a bag of cement," he told JoyNews.

The controversy has also extended to the aircraft's interior, following claims that it has a dedicated bedroom and bathroom.

But Ofosu dismissed claims that the jet had such luxury facilities, saying the president has no intention of "bathing in the air".

"There certainly is no bathroom. President Mahama has no intention of bathing in the air," Ofosu said.

He explained that the jet has reclining seats that can be converted into sleeping arrangements but denied that it has a dedicated bedroom.

The government says the new jet will replace the 16-year-old Falcon 900EX, which has suffered recurring maintenance problems, including corrosion and leakages in its fuel tank.

The older jet was reportedly grounded in France for several months in 2025 while undergoing repairs.

Officials say the Falcon 6X has a longer flying range, reducing the need for refuelling stops on international trips and improving the reliability of presidential travel.

Professor Godfred Alufar Bokpin, an economist at the University of Ghana said that while the president's safety was paramount, the timing of the purchase was difficult to justify amid severe austerity measures, high unemployment and widespread infrastructure challenges.

"The timing makes it a bit difficult to understand," he told the BBC, adding that the government should provide a cost-benefit analysis explaining why buying the jet was preferable to leasing one and how the decision serves Ghana's interests.

Additional reporting by Thomas Naadi in Accra

blocks.text: 图片来源：Ghana Air Force
图片说明，
官员称，这架法国制造的 Falcon 6X 将取代老化的总统专机
作者：Wycliffe Muia
更新于 3 小时前
加纳政府为其购买新总统专机辩护，尽管有人批评其成本，而许多公民仍在为高昂的生活费用挣扎。
这架价值6000万美元（4600万英镑）、法国制造的 Falcon 6X 引发了政治争议，反对派政客指责约翰·马哈马总统的政府轻重倒置。
但政府称此次采购是合理的，理由是加纳经济好转，这架飞机买得起，而且需要替换老化的总统专机。
这场争议出现之际，马哈马政府正试图证明经济已在多年财政困难并迫使加纳向 IMF 求援之后出现复苏。

items: 加纳新总统能否达到选民的高期望？发表于2025年1月7日

blocks.text: 这架由法国航空航天公司达索航空（Dassault Aviation）制造的飞机于周一交付给加纳空军，据报造价6100万美元。
议会去年 12 月批准了此次采购，作为加纳军事航空舰队现代化更广泛计划的一部分，该计划还包括四架 Airbus 直升机。
这架飞机周一抵达时受到喷水礼欢迎，但其到来在网上和反对派政客中引发了对其采购成本和时机的批评。
马哈马在野时曾本人反对购买新的总统专机，这引发了质疑：他的政府如今为何又推进这项采购。
反对党议员 Samuel Abu Jinapor 质疑政府的优先事项，称在许多加纳人仍在为生活成本挣扎、青年失业率仍高得惊人的时候，却出现了这笔开支。
Jinapor 还说：“在野时不可接受的事情，不能仅仅因为掌权者换了人，到了执政时就突然变得可以接受。”
他指责执政的全国民主大会党（NDC）虚伪，回顾该党高层在野时曾强烈反对为总统购置新飞机的提议。
吉纳波还呼吁提高采购流程、购机资金来源以及政府支出理由的透明度。

blocks.alt: Kenneth Adjei in a blue shirt inside a luxurious jet

blocks.text: 图片来源：Ghana Air Force
图片说明，
国防部长 Kenneth Adjei 周一迎接并检阅了这架新飞机
这笔采购也在社交媒体上引发尖锐批评，一些用户认为这些钱本可以花在更紧迫的公共需求上。
一名 X 用户发帖称：「这笔钱可以雇用超过 10 万名护士和 20 万名教师。」
但政府驳回了批评，称自全国民主大会党（NDC）反对类似采购以来，加纳的经济形势已发生很大变化。
议会国防委员会主席彼得·兰切内·图布表示，该党原则上从未反对购置总统专机。
他说，反对的理由是时机——当时加纳正经历严重的经济困难。
他说：「我们原则上同意需要采购一架新的总统专机。」
不过他辩称，加纳当时正在寻求国际货币基金组织 30 亿美元的救助，无法为这笔开支辩护。
他补充说：“这个国家的实力和宏观经济稳定提升了我们的地位，进口变得更便宜，现在正是合适的时机。”
图布说，政府在没有借贷的情况下购买了这架飞机，理由是加纳货币走强、经济状况改善。
政府发言人夸基耶·奥福苏也驳斥了此次采购属于优先事项错配的说法。
他指出，建材价格下降和借贷成本降低，证明该国经济状况有所改善。
他告诉 JoyNews：“我2024年竞选时捐赠水泥，一袋要115塞地（7.5英镑）。现在80塞地就能买到一袋水泥。”
争议还延伸到这架飞机的内部，有说法称机上设有专用卧室和浴室。
但 Ofosu 否认这架飞机有此类豪华设施，称总统无意“在空中洗澡”。
「当然没有浴室。马哈马总统无意在空中洗澡，」奥福苏说。
他解释说，这架飞机有可放倒并改成卧铺的座椅，但否认机上有独立卧室。
政府表示，新飞机将替换已使用 16 年的 Falcon 900EX，后者反复出现维护问题，包括腐蚀和油箱泄漏。
据报，那架较旧的飞机 2025 年在法国停飞数月进行维修。
官员称，Falcon 6X 航程更长，可减少国际行程中的加油经停，并提高总统出行的可靠性。

「这个时机让人有点难以理解，」他告诉 BBC，并补充说政府应提供成本效益分析，解释为何买下这架飞机比租赁更可取，以及该决定如何符合加纳的利益。

items.summary: Leaked documents raise questions about claims Egypt met welfare targets to qualify for €2.5bn in loans The European Commission has been accused of sugarcoating figures to enable it to release funds to Egypt under a landmark pact with the authoritarian government of Abdel Fatah al-Sisi. The charge re…
items.body:
Ursula von der Leyen and Abdel Fatah al-Sisi after a meeting in Cairo in March 2024. Photograph: Stavros Ioannides/PIO/AFP/Getty Images

Ursula von der Leyen and Abdel Fatah al-Sisi after a meeting in Cairo in March 2024. Photograph: Stavros Ioannides/PIO/AFP/Getty Images

European Commission accused of sugarcoating figures to release funds to Egypt

Leaked documents raise questions about claims Egypt met welfare targets to qualify for €2.5bn in loans

The European Commission has been accused of sugarcoating figures to enable it to release funds to Egypt under a landmark pact with the authoritarian government of Abdel Fatah al-Sisi.

The charge relates to a €7.4bn deal promised by Ursula von der Leyen, the European Commission president, to al-Sisi on a high-profile visit to Cairo in 2024. The three-year “strategic and comprehensive partnership” was intended to bolster Egypt’s shaky economy, deter migrants from coming to Europe and shore up a region reeling from the 7 October attacks and Israel’s war on Gaza.

The disclosure raises broader questions about the EU-Egypt relationship, as Egyptian authorities face scrutiny over shrinking press freedom following the jailing and alleged torture of six journalists, the entire newsroom of Matsadaash, a factchecking and investigative platform, and the closure last month of one of the country’s last independent news outlets and conviction of its high-profile editor, Lina Attalah.

Attalah is appealing against that conviction and will be in court this week as she seeks to overturn other charges including “publishing false news”, for which she was sentenced to a year in prison in absentia without her knowledge.

The spotlight is on €5bn in EU “soft” loans to Egypt – lending with easy repayment terms, known as macro-financial assistance, that is meant to be available only to countries that respect human rights and democracy. While the EU conditions on democracy and rights are vague, the loans impose much more specific requirements on Egypt to carry out economic reforms.

Separate data sources – from leaked EU documents and deleted from an Egyptian government website – raise questions about the European Commission’s claims that Egypt met targets linked to social welfare programmes, which enabled the EU to release €2.5bn in assistance.

In confidential documents, the commission told EU lawmakers that Egypt had “broadly fulfilled” and then “fulfilled” two separate targets to increase the numbers of poor people on social welfare programmes between 2024 and 2026. But data points to a net reduction of 85,734 households as the Egyptian government removed people from its welfare programmes rather than expanded coverage.

If Egypt had expanded the programmes in line with the EU’s apparent conditions – and not removed any households – about 245,000 households, equivalent to roughly 909,000 people, would be getting these benefits. (The Guardian used World Bank data to make this rough calculation).

According to the leaked documents, the commission wanted Egypt to “further expand cash transfer programmes”, but despite a net reduction in beneficiaries it gave the green light anyway to two separate “soft” loans totalling €2.5bn.

In response to the Guardian’s findings, one of the European parliament’s leading spokespeople on EU-Egypt relations, the Dutch MEP Tineke Strik, said she was introducing a question to the European Commission demanding clarification.

“The finding by this investigation that the commission is seemingly sugarcoating Egypt’s performance is worrying,” Strik said. “From the beginning, the commission has used macro-financial assistance primarily as a tool to lure Egypt into migration cooperation, while considering formal conditions and its reporting obligations towards parliament as an inconvenient formality.”

A street scene in Cairo. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images

Under the plan, Egypt has so far received €3.5bn in soft loans in three instalments, with a final payment of €1.5bn expected before the end of 2027.

The charge of sugarcoating figures relates to two social welfare programmes: the Takaful and Karama cash transfer programmes for poor and vulnerable households.

The Takaful (Solidarity) programme gives poor families cash payments as long as recipients have regular health visits and good attendance at school. The Karama (Dignity) programme gives unconditional cash payments to people living with a disability, older people, orphans and widows.

One of the EU conditions for Egypt to gain the first €1bn loan was to increase the number of Takaful and Karama beneficiary households by 100,000 to 4.7 million.

In a leaked report to lawmakers in the EU council of ministers and the European parliament, the commission described that requirement as “broadly fulfilled”.

The data in that report, however, reveals a net fall of 62,281 households during this period, owing to what the EU officials describe as “a multi-annual recertification process”. Some beneficiaries were added to the list but a larger number were removed because they were deemed ineligible.

In order to achieve a later instalment of €1.5bn, Egypt was required to “further expand” the programmes, adding 60,000 households to the Takaful and Karama beneficiaries list. A second leaked report to EU lawmakers shows that the commission concluded the target was “fulfilled” because 442,118 families were added to the list.

On this occasion, the commission did not report on numbers removed. Figures from Egypt’s ministry of social solidarity, however, show a net reduction of 23,453 beneficiaries to the programmes in the 11 months until June 2026, the period leading up to the release of that payment. The EU announced the release of the €1.5bn payment in July 2026.

The data has since been deleted from the Egyptian ministry website but the Guardian has seen screenshots and archived webpages.

During a period from 2024 to 26 when the EU required Egypt to add 160,000 households to the rolls of the Karama and Takaful programmes, there was a net decline of 85,734 households.

A customer pays for tomatoes with Egyptian pound banknotes at a market in Cairo. Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty Images

Timothy Kaldas, the deputy director of the Tahrir Institute for Middle East Policy, said the commission had generally “done a poor job of leveraging the funds of European taxpayers to support genuine stabilisation” on the other side of the Mediterranean. “The strategic interest of Europe is seeing a more economically stable Egypt with a population that is less precarious,” he said.

Sandra Gómez López, a Spanish socialist MEP who recently visited Cairo to assess human rights in Egypt, said the data presented by the Guardian raised important questions. “The commission must explain transparently why it considers these commitments to have been fulfilled and demonstrate that European funding is genuinely contributing to improving social protection for the Egyptian population,” she said.

She stressed that the EU should not withdraw support, “but neither can we allow the country’s strategic importance to lead us to lower our standards when it comes to human rights”.

For critics, the questions about the EU’s willingness to hold Egypt accountable on very precise socioeconomic targets do not bode well for the broader but less defined goals for democracy and human rights.

Strik said: “The fact that Egypt and the commission even seem to ignore the crystal-clear socioeconomic conditions doesn’t increase my expectation that they adhere to the vague precondition on democracy and the rule of law.”

Claudio Francavilla, an associate EU director at Human Rights Watch, said: “Without benchmarks, the EU has turned a human rights conditionality into a blank cheque for Egypt’s authoritarianism.”

In a statement to the Guardian, the European Commission said the policy target on Takaful and Karama referred to new beneficiary families “and not to its net increase”. The spokesperson said there was “no contradiction” between this statement and that in a confidential document that said Egypt was required to “further expand cash transfer programmes”.

Asked about the release of the remaining €1.5bn in promised loans, the commission said it “will be made once all conditions have been met”, referring to 24 economic policy conditions, keeping an IMF programme on track and “taking concrete and credible steps towards respecting effective democratic mechanisms, including a multiparty parliamentary system, and the rule of law, and guaranteeing respect for human rights”.

It added: “Compliance with the conditionality is examined thoroughly” by EU officials and diplomats based on “information provided by the Egyptian authorities and other relevant sources”.

Egypt’s mission to the EU in Brussels did not respond to a request for comment.
