blocks.text: 乌尔苏拉·冯德莱恩与阿卜杜勒·法塔赫·塞西2024年3月在开罗会晤后。照片：Stavros Ioannides/PIO/AFP/Getty Images
乌尔苏拉·冯德莱恩与阿卜杜勒·法塔赫·塞西2024年3月在开罗会晤后。照片：Stavros Ioannides/PIO/AFP/Getty Images
欧盟委员会被指粉饰数据以向埃及拨款
泄露文件对埃及已达成福利目标从而有资格获得 25 亿欧元贷款的说法提出质疑
欧盟委员会被指责粉饰数据，以便根据与 Abdel Fatah al-Sisi 威权政府达成的一项里程碑式协议，向埃及拨付资金。
这项指控涉及欧盟委员会主席乌尔苏拉·冯德莱恩2024年高调访问开罗时向塞西承诺的一笔74亿欧元交易。为期三年的“战略全面伙伴关系”旨在支撑埃及脆弱的经济、阻止移民前往欧洲，并稳固因10月7日袭击和以色列对加沙战争而动荡的地区。
这一披露给欧盟与埃及的关系提出了更广泛的问题，因为埃及当局正因新闻自由萎缩而受到审视：六名记者遭到监禁并据称遭受酷刑，他们是事实核查与调查平台 Matsadaash 的整个新闻编辑室；上个月该国仅存的独立新闻机构之一被关闭，其知名主编 Lina Attalah 被判有罪。
Attalah 正在对该项定罪提出上诉，本周还将出庭，寻求推翻包括「发布虚假新闻」在内的其他指控；她曾在本人不知情的情况下被缺席判处一年监禁。
外界关注的是欧盟向埃及提供的50亿欧元“软”贷款——还款条件宽松的贷款，称为宏观财政援助，原则上只应提供给尊重人权和民主的国家。欧盟在民主和权利方面的条件含糊，但这些贷款对埃及实施经济改革提出了具体得多的要求。
来自泄露的欧盟文件以及从埃及政府网站上删除的内容等不同数据来源，让人对欧盟委员会关于埃及已达到社会福利项目相关目标的说法产生疑问；正是这些目标使欧盟得以发放 25 亿欧元援助。
在机密文件中，委员会告诉欧盟立法者，埃及在2024年至2026年间“大体完成”、随后又“完成”了两项互不相关的目标，即增加社会福利项目中贫困人口的数量。但数据显示，家庭净减少了85,734户，因为埃及政府是在把人从福利项目中移除，而不是扩大覆盖面。
如果埃及按照欧盟表面上的条件扩大这些项目——并且没有移除任何家庭——约 24.5 万户家庭、相当于大约 90.9 万人将获得这些福利。（《卫报》使用世界银行数据作出这一粗略计算。）
根据泄露的文件，欧盟委员会希望埃及「进一步扩大现金转移项目」，但尽管受益人数净减少，委员会还是为两笔总计 25 亿欧元的「软」贷款开了绿灯。
针对《卫报》的调查结果，欧洲议会在欧盟-埃及关系方面的主要发言人之一、荷兰议员 Tineke Strik 表示，她将向欧盟委员会提出质询，要求予以澄清。
“这项调查发现，委员会似乎在粉饰埃及的表现，这令人担忧，”Strik 说。“从一开始，委员会就把宏观财政援助主要当作把埃及拉入移民合作的工具，而把正式条件及其对议会的报告义务视为一种不便的形式。”

blocks.alt: People, vehicles and market stalls in a street in Cairo

blocks.text: 开罗的街景。照片：Anadolu/Getty Images
根据该计划，埃及迄今已分三期获得35亿欧元优惠贷款，最后一笔15亿欧元预计将在2027年底前支付。
粉饰数据的指控涉及两项社会福利计划：面向贫困和弱势家庭的 Takaful 和 Karama 现金转移支付计划。
“互助”（Takaful）项目向贫困家庭提供现金补助，条件是受助者定期就医且就学出勤良好。“尊严”（Karama）项目则向残疾人、老年人、孤儿和寡妇提供无条件现金补助。
埃及获得首笔10亿欧元贷款的欧盟条件之一，是将 Takaful 和 Karama 计划的受益家庭增加10万户，达到470万户。
在一份泄露给欧盟部长理事会和欧洲议会立法者的报告中，欧盟委员会称该要求“大体上已经满足”。
然而，该报告中的数据显示，在此期间家庭数量净减少 62,281 户，原因是欧盟官员所说的“多年重新核验程序”。一些受益人被列入名单，但更多人因被认定不符合资格而被移除。
为获得后续 15 亿欧元的款项，埃及被要求“进一步扩大”这些项目，在 Takaful 和 Karama 受益名单上再增加 6 万户家庭。另一份泄露给欧盟议员的报告显示，欧盟委员会认定该目标已“完成”，因为名单上新增了 442,118 个家庭。
这一次，委员会没有报告被移除的人数。不过，埃及社会团结部的数据显示，在截至2026年6月的11个月里——也就是这笔款项发放前的时期——这些项目的受益人净减少了23,453人。欧盟于2026年7月宣布发放这笔15亿欧元款项。
跳过新闻通讯推广
新闻通讯推广之后
这些数据此后已从埃及政府部门网站上删除，但《卫报》看到过截图和存档网页。
在2024年至26年期间，欧盟要求埃及将16万户家庭纳入 Karama 和 Takaful 项目名册，但实际净减少了85734户。

blocks.alt: A person hands over Egyptian banknotes to a tomato seller

blocks.text: 一名顾客在开罗市场用埃及镑钞票购买番茄。照片：Bloomberg/Getty Images
塔利尔中东政策研究所副所长 Timothy Kaldas 说，委员会总体上“在利用欧洲纳税人的资金支持地中海对岸真正的稳定方面做得很差”。“欧洲的战略利益在于看到一个经济更稳定、人口不那么岌岌可危的埃及，”他说。
最近前往开罗评估埃及人权状况的西班牙社会党欧洲议会议员 Sandra Gómez López 说，《卫报》出示的数据提出了重要问题。“委员会必须透明地解释，为何认为这些承诺已经兑现，并证明欧洲资金确实在改善埃及人口的社会保护方面作出贡献，”她说。
她强调，欧盟不应撤回支持，“但我们也不能因为该国的战略重要性，就在人权问题上降低标准”。
在批评者看来，欧盟是否愿意就非常具体的社会经济目标追究埃及责任的问题，对更宽泛、定义更模糊的民主和人权目标而言并非好兆头。
Strik 说：「埃及和欧盟委员会甚至似乎无视那些清晰明确的社会经济条件，这并不会让我更期待他们会遵守关于民主与法治的模糊前提。」
Human Rights Watch 的欧盟事务副主管 Claudio Francavilla 说：“没有衡量标准，欧盟就把人权附加条件变成了给埃及威权主义的一张空白支票。”
在给《卫报》的声明中，欧盟委员会表示，Takaful 和 Karama 的政策目标指的是新增受益家庭，“而不是其净增加”。发言人说，这一表述与一份机密文件中要求埃及“进一步扩大现金转移项目”的说法“并不矛盾”。

它还补充说：欧盟官员和外交官会根据“埃及当局及其他相关来源提供的信息”，“彻底审查对附加条件的遵守情况”。
埃及驻布鲁塞尔欧盟使团未回应置评请求。

items.title: Waymo pulls driverless taxis from all US freeways
items.summary: The decision comes after California banned Waymo's driverless vehicles from operating on the state's highways following a series of traffic incidents.
items.body:
Image source, Brandon Bell / Getty Images

ByJames Chater

Waymo has temporarily suspended its driverless vehicles from operating on all US freeways, the company has said.

The decision comes after California banned Waymo's driverless taxis from state freeways following a series of recent traffic incidents.

California's Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) cited an "imminent hazard to public safety" for the ban, noting an incident this month in which several driverless Waymo vehicles entered an active construction zone on US Route 101.

Waymo said it was working with state officials "diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations", adding that no injuries or collisions were reported following the incident on US Route 101 south of San Francisco.

California's DMV said Waymo's driverless taxis presented a risk "due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present".

In another incident earlier this month, footage widely seen on social media appeared to show a Waymo car trying to overtake patrol vehicles that were deliberately slowing the pace of traffic on a San Francisco highway.

The California ban, which came into effect on 11 November, would remain in place until Waymo "demonstrates to the department that it has taken effective corrective actions to address the deficiencies that precipitated the restrictions".

A Waymo spokesperson said: "In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance."

Data on Waymo's website suggests that its cars, compared to human drivers, are involved in 95% fewer crashes resulting in serious injury.

Waymo currently operates driverless taxis in 15 US cities, but only offered freeway rides in a handful of those locations, including San Francisco, Los Angeles and Miami.

The company's driverless taxis can continue to operate on regular city streets.

In May, Waymo recalled thousands of its self-driving cars in the US over a software issue that could allow vehicles to drive into flooded roads.

In the same month, multiple Waymo cars were spotted driving around a cul-de-sac in Atlanta, Georgia, in the early hours of the morning.

blocks.alt: A Waymo taxi charges up at a charging station in Austin, Texas in January.

blocks.text: 图片来源：Brandon Bell / Getty Images
作者：James Chater
Waymo 表示，已暂时暂停其无人驾驶车辆在美国所有高速公路上运行。
此前，加州在一系列交通事故后禁止 Waymo 无人驾驶出租车进入州际高速公路，随后作出了这一决定。
加州机动车管理局（DMV）以「对公共安全构成迫在眉睫的危害」为由实施了这项禁令，并提到本月发生的一起事件：几辆无人驾驶的 Waymo 车辆驶入了美国 101 号公路上一个正在施工的区域。
Waymo 表示，正在与州官员“勤勉而负责任地合作，以恢复高速公路运营”，并补充说，旧金山以南美国 101 号公路上的事件发生后，没有人员受伤或碰撞的报告。
加州机动车管理局（DMV）表示，Waymo 的无人驾驶出租车构成风险，“原因是其车辆一再闯入有施工人员、车辆和设备的在建施工区域”。
本月早些时候的另一起事件中，社交媒体上广泛传播的视频似乎显示，一辆 Waymo 汽车试图超越在旧金山高速公路上故意放慢车流的巡警车辆。
加州这项于 11 月 11 日生效的禁令将持续有效，直到 Waymo「向该部门证明，已采取有效纠正措施，解决导致这些限制的缺陷」。
Waymo 一位发言人说：“本着安全第一的原则，我们也已暂时限制其他运营市场的高速公路运行，以评估我们的表现。”
Waymo 网站上的数据显示，与人类驾驶员相比，其车辆造成严重伤害的事故减少了95%。
Waymo 目前在 15 个美国城市运营无人驾驶出租车，但仅在其中少数地点提供高速公路行程，包括旧金山、洛杉矶和迈阿密。
该公司的无人驾驶出租车可以继续在普通城市街道上运营。
今年5月，Waymo 在美国召回了数千辆自动驾驶汽车，原因是一项软件问题可能导致车辆驶入被淹道路。
同月，有人发现多辆 Waymo 汽车在乔治亚州亚特兰大一条死胡同里于凌晨来回行驶。

items.body:
South Korea’s university exam, known as the suneung, runs for a gruelling eight hours over a single day and determines which university candidates can attend. Photograph: Kim Hong-Ji/Reuters

South Korea’s university exam, known as the suneung, runs for a gruelling eight hours over a single day and determines which university candidates can attend. Photograph: Kim Hong-Ji/Reuters

South Korea’s high-stakes university exams upended by AI cheating scandal

South Korea has been gripped by revelations of AI-aided cheating, just days before more than half a million students are to sit high-stakes entrance exams

The integrity of South Korea’s career-defining university entrance exam has been thrown into doubt after the top scorer in a recent professional exam admitted using a concealed camera and AI to cheat.

On Thursday, more than half a million people, mostly school students, are due to sit the exam, known as the suneung, at 1,312 centres across the country. The exam runs for a gruelling eight hours over a single day and determines which university a candidate can attend and, in turn, their future prospects.

The country goes to great lengths to ensure the smooth running of the suneung. Aircraft take-offs and landings are rescheduled during the 25-minute English listening paper to minimise noise, while artillery fire and tank movements are suspended.

The stock market opens an hour late and cars are stopped 200 metres from every centre. Extra trains run from 6am, police drive latecomers to their exam halls, and tourist attractions open late to ease traffic. Offices are asked to open at 10am.

160 questions, only one wrong: top scorer in South Korea tax exam admits AI cheating

Read more

But in recent days, exam organisers have faced a renewed threat to the validity of the entire exercise, after the top scorer in this year’s tax accountancy exam- who got just one question wrong out of 160– admitted on Sunday he had cheated by using AI.

Prime minister Han Seong-sook told a cabinet meeting in Seoul on Tuesday that AI-assisted cheating was a “social evil” that the government would “root out”.

“We will block outright the carrying of smart devices during the exam,” she said. The education ministry and other agencies should approach it “as if staking their jobs on it”, she added.

Han said smart devices must be turned off and handed in, while bags left in corridors would be checked for any devices that were still on. Exam officials would also inspect all candidates’ glasses and watches, as well as their collars, sleeves and buttons for concealed cameras.

The government will also send emergency alerts to every phone in the country, which sound at full volume and cannot be silenced, in the hope of catching out anyone who has not handed in their device.

More invigilators will be deployed, and the government said it was preparing to switch off school wifi inside exam centres and public wifi nearby, and that personal hotspots, which cannot be blocked, would be traced through connection records.

The weekend’s cheating revelation captured national headlines in South Korea, stoking concern about the security of the suneung.

In a video posted to his lawyer’s YouTube channel, the exam cheat said he had photographed the questions with a concealed microcamera, sent them to an AI system and read the answers from a smartphone. “I cheated in the tax accountant exam,” he said. “My top placing is not the result of legitimate effort.”

South Korean education minister Choi Kyo-jin reviews the method used to cheat in the national tax accountant exam. Photograph: Seo Dae-yeon/YONHAP/AP

His lawyer handed police a camera, a laptop and a phone. No charges have been brought, and the prime minister has ordered procedures to begin that would void his result and bar him for five years.

The education minister, Choi Kyo-jin, told parliament on Monday that while authorities could screen out the smart glasses already on sale at Thursday’s exam, newer variants could not be dealt with perfectly.

Choi has ruled out postponing the exam, which has been delayed several times before, including in 2017, after an earthquake struck the south-eastern city of Pohang, and in 2020 due to the Covid pandemic.

Smart glasses have been banned in exams since the end of June. In October, several candidates were caught with them while sitting university-run admissions exams. At the suneung, wearing a pair counts as using one even when switched off.

The education ministry looked at using radio-frequency equipment to detect the glasses in exam halls, but concluded conditions varied too much between venues for deployment this year. Checks will instead rely on visual inspection, with at least one dedicated official placed in each exam centre.

Workers process packages of question-and-answer sheets for South Korea’s university entrance exams on 16 November. Photograph: YONHAP/EPA

Teachers’ unions have criticised the government response as belated. A survey last month of 2,716 secondary school teachers by the Korean Teachers and Education Workers Union showed that 82.3% said they could not tell whether a candidate was wearing smart glasses under the current procedure, with only 3.5% saying they could.

To avoid facing scrutiny on exam day, some candidates are reportedly switching to contact lenses. An optician in Suwon, south of Seoul, said students who had never worn contacts were coming in to ask how to put them in.

Han said on X on Monday that the checks would be handled carefully “so that candidates acting in good faith do not suffer unnecessary anxiety or inconvenience”.

In his video confession, the accountancy test cheat addressed suneung candidates directly. “The suneung is coming up soon,” he said.

“To anyone thinking of cheating as I did: I am going to tell the investigators everything, so please don’t think, ‘I won’t get caught.’”

就在超过50万名学生即将参加高风险入学考试的几天前，韩国被人工智能辅助作弊的曝光所震动
韩国这场决定职业生涯的大学入学考试的诚信受到质疑：近日一场专业考试的最高分得主承认，使用了隐蔽摄像头和人工智能作弊。
周四，全国 1,312 个考点将有逾 50 万人（主要是在校学生）参加被称为 suneung（高考）的考试。考试在一天内进行，长达八小时，极为艰苦，决定着考生能进入哪所大学，进而影响其前途。
韩国为确保高考（suneung）顺利举行不遗余力。在25分钟英语听力考试期间，飞机起降时间被重新安排以减少噪音，炮击和坦克机动也暂停。
股市晚一小时开盘，车辆在每个考场200米外停驶。从早上6点加开列车，警察开车送迟到考生前往考场，旅游景点延后开放以缓解交通。办公场所被要求10点上班。

但近几天，考试组织者再次面临整个考试有效性的威胁：今年税务会计考试的最高分得主——160题中只错一题——周日承认自己使用了人工智能作弊。
总理 Han Seong-sook 周二在首尔的内阁会议上表示，人工智能辅助作弊是政府将“铲除”的“社会毒瘤”。
“我们将彻底禁止在考试期间携带智能设备，”她说。她还表示，教育部和其他机构应以“好像乌纱帽都押在这上面”的态度来对待此事。
韩某表示，智能设备必须关闭并上交，留在走廊的包袋将检查是否仍有开机设备。考务人员还将检查所有考生的眼镜和手表，以及衣领、袖口和纽扣，以防隐藏摄像头。
政府还将向全国每一部手机发送紧急警报，警报会以最大音量响起且无法静音，希望借此抓住尚未上交设备的人。
将增派更多监考人员，政府还表示正准备关闭考场内的学校 wifi 以及附近的公共 wifi，并称无法屏蔽的个人热点将通过连接记录进行追踪。
周末曝光的作弊事件登上韩国全国头条，引发了对修能考试（suneung）安全的担忧。
在其律师 YouTube 频道发布的视频中，这名作弊考生称，他用隐藏的微型摄像头拍摄试题，发送给一套 AI 系统，再从智能手机上读取答案。“我在税务会计师考试中作弊了，”他说，“我拿到的第一名并不是正当努力的结果。”

blocks.text: 韩国教育部长 Choi Kyo-jin 检查国家税务会计师考试中的作弊方法。照片：Seo Dae-yeon/YONHAP/AP
他的律师向警方交出了一台摄像机、一台笔记本电脑和一部手机。目前尚未提出指控，总理已下令启动程序，将取消其成绩并禁止其五年内再考。
教育部长崔教珍周一告诉议会，虽然当局可以在周四的考试中筛除已经在售的智能眼镜，但较新的变体无法被完美应对。
崔已排除推迟考试的可能。该考试此前曾多次延期，包括2017年东南部城市浦项发生地震之后，以及2020年因新冠疫情。
智能眼镜自 6 月底起就被禁止带入考场。10 月，有数名考生在参加大学举办的招生考试时被发现佩戴。在韩国高考（suneung）中，即使处于关闭状态，戴上一副也算使用。
教育部曾考虑在考场使用射频设备检测这类眼镜，但认为各考点条件差异太大，今年无法部署。检查将改靠目视，每个考点至少安排一名专职人员。

blocks.text: 11月16日，工作人员处理韩国高考答题卡。照片：YONHAP/EPA
教师工会批评政府的应对来得太迟。韩国教师与教育工作者工会上个月对 2,716 名中学教师的调查显示，82.3% 的人表示，按现行程序无法判断考生是否戴了智能眼镜，只有 3.5% 的人表示能够判断。

韩周一在 X 上表示，审查将谨慎处理，“以免出于善意行事的候选人遭受不必要的焦虑或不便”。
在视频忏悔中，这名会计考试作弊者直接对修能考试（suneung）考生说话。“修能考试马上就要到了，”他说。

items.title: Nvidia says it won't reinstate Huang as it reports soaring sales
items.summary: The AI chip giant reported strong quarterly earnings on Tuesday after the dramatic exit of Jensen Huang.
items.body:
Image source, Getty/Nvidia via Reuters

Image caption,

Jensen Huang and Nvidia's interim CEO, Colette Kress

ByKali Hays, Technology reporter and Osmond Chia, Business reporter

Updated 18 November 2026 01:18 GMT

Nvidia has firmly ruled out letting ousted co-founder Jensen Huang return as it revealed that sales doubled to more than $100bn.

In the company's first results since Huang's dramatic exit last week, covering the three month period just before the recent scandal surfaced, interim chief executive Colette Kress said it was "business as usual". She told investors: "We've got this."

Earlier on Tuesday, Huang said he would be "honoured" to return and lead Nvidia, having quit following alleged extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected spy for China.

But Nvidia's chair Harvey Jones said: "The board does not intend to reinstate him."

Nvidia reported that sales for the three months to 25 October rose to $115.8bn (£86.9bn), with shares in the company jumping by 4.8% in after-hours trading.

The company's profits also doubled from a year ago rising to $65bn. Sales from data centres, a significant part of Nvidia's business, also doubled to $107bn.

The company said its rapid growth is poised to continue and revenue will rise by another 13% in the next quarter.

• How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?Published7 hours ago

Given the uncertainty surrounding the company after Huang's exit, financial analysts had been unsure that Nvidia would provide any forward-looking guidance.

Daniela Hathorn, a senior analyst for trading platform Capital.com, said Nvidia's results "offer a strong answer to concerns that demand for AI infrastructure is cooling" and temper immediate worries that Huang was irreplaceable as a leader.

"The harder question is whether Nvidia can preserve the strategic advantage Huang helped build," Hathorn added. "His exit is unlikely to change orders already committed, but could matter more when Nvidia makes its next round of decisions on products, partnerships and investment."

Figure caption,

Watch: Who is suspected Chinese spy at centre of Nvidia affair investigation?

Kress seemed eager to stress that Nvidia can continue to not only succeed, but lead the ongoing AI buildout that is happening throughout the technology industry.

"It is business as usual," she said. "Our partners, our suppliers, all of them are 100% behind us."

She added that Nvidia's leadership team has "stood up very strongly over the last week... working seamlessly in all of their departments and projects".

"Our momentum is real. Our demand is accelerating. Our supply is growing. Our customers and our partners are with us, and employees are committed." Kress said before leaving the analyst call. "We've got this."

The interim chief executive also said Nvidia is no longer shipping Hopper data centre semiconductors to China.

The Hopper technology is in Nvidia's advanced H200 processors, which the firm won approval to sell in China after Huang's repeated lobbying efforts in Washington.

They had previously been restricted over concerns that selling them to China would give its industries and military an edge over the US.

Kress did not elaborate on why the shipments had been stopped.

• The rise and fall of Jensen Huang - how the tech superstar became mired in scandalPublished5 days ago

• Jensen Huang says he would be 'honoured' to return as Nvidia CEO if board asked himPublished18 hours ago

Jones saying earlier that the company would not answer analysts' questions about Huang or Nvidia's investigation into his conduct, he did address the search for a permanent replacement.

He said Nvidia is working with an executive search firm and is considering internal and external candidates, but that the company would not rush its selection.

"With the advanced technology and the national security dynamics in the marketplace, our new chief executive will have to navigate those waters carefully," Jones said. "The search will be thorough and we want to do it as quickly as possible, but we won't do it before we find the exact right person."

Michael Monaghan from investment firm Founder ETFs is among those who want Huang back in the top job at Nvidia.

The Nvidia investor told the BBC that he is waiting to see the results of a thorough investigation into Huang's actions, instead of relying on "salacious allegations" made in the media.

Nvidia's strong earnings are "from the machine that Jensen built" and a company tends to lose "its shine and vision" after an iconic founder leaves, Monaghan said.

作者：Kali Hays（科技记者）和 Osmond Chia（商业记者）

Nvidia 明确排除让被罢免的联合创始人黄仁勋回归的可能，同时公布销售额已翻倍至超过 1000 亿美元。
在黄仁勋上周戏剧性离职后的首份业绩中，覆盖近期丑闻曝光前的三个月，临时首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯表示“一切照常”。她对投资者说：“我们能搞定。”
周二早些时候，Huang 表示，若能重返并领导 Nvidia，他将深感“荣幸”。他此前因被指婚外情——其中包括与一名疑似中国间谍的关系——而辞职。
但 Nvidia 董事长 Harvey Jones 表示：「董事会不打算让他复职。」
Nvidia 报告称，截至10月25日的三个月销售额升至1158亿美元（869亿英镑），该公司股价在盘后交易中上涨4.8%。
该公司利润也较一年前翻倍，升至650亿美元。作为 Nvidia 业务重要组成部分的数据中心销售额同样翻倍，达到1070亿美元。
该公司表示，快速增长有望持续，下一季度营收还将再增长 13%。

items.title: Pakistani man sentenced to 27 years in US prison over Trump murder plot
items.summary: Asif Merchant, allegedly linked to Iran, found by court to have sought retribution over Qassem Suleimani death A Pakistani man was sentenced to more than 27 years in prison on Tuesday for plotting to assassinate Donald Trump in retaliation for the US killing of Revolutionary Guards commander Qassem…
items.body:
Asif Merchant, in this court sketch. Photograph: Jane Rosenberg/Reuters

Asif Merchant, in this court sketch. Photograph: Jane Rosenberg/Reuters

Pakistani man sentenced to 27 years in US prison over Trump murder plot

Asif Merchant, allegedly linked to Iran, found by court to have sought retribution over Qassem Suleimani death

A Pakistani man was sentenced to more than 27 years in prison on Tuesday for plotting to assassinate Donald Trump in retaliation for the US killing of Revolutionary Guards commander Qassem Suleimani, the Department of Justice said.

Asif Merchant, who had alleged ties to Iran, sought to hire a hitman to assassinate a politician or a government official in the United States, a Brooklyn court found.

Suleimani, the head of Iran’s foreign military operations, was killed in a US drone strike in Baghdad in January 2020. Iranian officials have repeatedly vowed to avenge his killing.

Merchant had testified that he was forced into the plot to protect his family in the Iranian capital Tehran from the Guards, adding that he thought he would get caught before anyone was killed, multiple media outlets reported.

He said he was never ordered to kill a specific person but noted his Iranian contact had mentioned three people in connection with the plot – Trump, the former US president Joe Biden and former UN ambassador Nikki Haley.

But the United States attorney general, Todd Blanche, insisted on Tuesday that the plot was against Donald Trump.

“An Iranian agent who came to the United States to coordinate an assassination attempt against President Trump has been justly sentenced for his criminal conduct,” said Blanche after Merchant was sentenced to 330 months’ imprisonment.

“The Department of Justice will not tolerate foreign terrorist plots against our leaders and will not stop until those responsible are held accountable.”

US officials previously said Merchant had “close ties to Iran” and described his alleged plot as “straight out of the Iranian regime’s playbook”.

Merchant was arrested on 12 July 2024 as he planned to leave the country.

items.title: Israeli parliament elects new speaker backed by Netanyahu’s opponents
items.summary: Knesset’s appointment of Matan Kahana marks step towards reversing policies of outgoing government The Israeli parliament elected a new speaker on Tuesday, a key step toward rolling back policies passed by the outgoing government led by the prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu. The new speaker is Mata…

Matan Kahana is an ally of Gadi Eisenkot, the party leader working to form the next government and replace Netanyahu. Photograph: Ohad Zwigenberg/AP

Matan Kahana is an ally of Gadi Eisenkot, the party leader working to form the next government and replace Netanyahu. Photograph: Ohad Zwigenberg/AP

Israeli parliament elects new speaker backed by Netanyahu’s opponents

Knesset’s appointment of Matan Kahana marks step towards reversing policies of outgoing government

The Israeli parliament elected a new speaker on Tuesday, a key step toward rolling back policies passed by the outgoing government led by the prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu.

The new speaker is Matan Kahana, an ally of Gadi Eisenkot, the party leader currently working to form the next government and replace Netanyahu.

Eisenkot’s bloc has pledged to undo some of Netanyahu’s most contentious policies following Kahana’s election.

He was approved as speaker with 66 votes in the 120-member chamber, backed by the Jewish-led opposition parties and by the Arab-led parties. The candidate backed by Netanyahu’s bloc, Ofir Katz, received 52 votes following a stormy debate that stretched over seven hours.

Eisenkot condemns Netanyahu’s ‘racist’ campaign against Israel’s Arab citizens

Read more

“The appointment of Matan Kahana as Knesset speaker is a worthy democratic move that reflects the absolute majority in favour of change,” Eisenkot said ahead of the vote.

The vote took place weeks after the parliamentary elections on 27 October in which Netanyahu and his allies lost their parliamentary majority. Eisenkot was subsequently tasked by Israel’s president with trying to form a new coalition government.

Eisenkot has up to five more weeks to secure enough alliances to form a coalition.

As negotiations continue on the sidelines, his bloc, along with unaffiliated Arab-led parties, can use their majority in the newly sworn-in Knesset to advance their legislative agenda.

They introduced several bills last week, including to set term limits on the role of prime minister, to form a government-led inquiry into the Hamas-led 7 October 2023 attacks and to reverse laws that limit the powers of the judiciary.

Kahana gives the opposition bloc a major legislative advantage, according to Assaf Shapira of the Israel Democracy Institute, a Jerusalem thinktank.

“It’s important because there is not much time, because the speaker of the Knesset can make the legislative process much, much faster or much slower,” Shapira said.

Kahana replaced Amir Ohana, a Netanyahu ally, as speaker.

Gadi Eisenkot is tasked with trying to form a new Israeli government. Photograph: Abir Sultan/EPA

Eisenkot and his allies are under pressure to swiftly advance their legislative priorities in the weeks ahead. Roy Folkman, a member of Eisenkot’s Yashar party, heads the temporary committee that decides much of the Knesset’s work until a government is formed.

If Eisenkot fails to form a government, the Israeli president could give Netanyahu an opportunity to do so. That would probably give Netanyahu’s Likud party control of the committee.

Even though Netanyahu’s opponents would still hold a majority, they would “feel that their momentum has gone”, Shapira said, and there would be a “real danger that some of the legislation will be delayed”.

Chamber procedures will pose a further challenge. A bill has to be introduced on the floor, considered in committee and voted on several times on the floor before it passes the Knesset. That winding process could make it hard to move bills across the finish line before time runs out.

Shapira said Eisenkot and his allies are likely to prioritise rolling back controversial laws that gave the government a larger role in appointing judges and weakened the power of Israel’s attorney general, an independent role that is seen by many as central to Israel’s system of government checks and balances.

“It’s very easy to abolish these laws because no new institution has to be created,” he said.

Establishing a body to investigate the 7 October attacks would be easier, Shapira added, and carry greater legitimacy once a government is formed.

Netanyahu’s opponents argue he has blocked an independent probe into any military or intelligence failures around the day, the deadliest in Israel’s history, and evaded accountability.

以色列议会任命Matan Kahana，标志着朝着扭转卸任政府政策迈出一步
以色列议会周二选出新议长，这是朝着撤回即将卸任、由总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡领导的政府所通过政策迈出的关键一步。
新议长是Matan Kahana，他是Gadi Eisenkot的盟友；Eisenkot是目前正在着手组建下届政府、取代内塔尼亚胡的政党领袖。
Eisenkot所属阵营已承诺，在Kahana当选后，将撤销内塔尼亚胡部分最具争议的政策。
他在这个120席的议院中以66票获批担任议长，得到犹太裔领导的反对党和阿拉伯裔领导的党派支持。内塔尼亚胡阵营支持的候选人Ofir Katz，在一场持续逾七小时的激烈辩论后获得52票。
艾森科特谴责内塔尼亚胡针对以色列阿拉伯公民的“种族主义”竞选活动
阅读更多
“任命Matan Kahana为以色列议会议长，是一项值得肯定的民主举措，反映了支持变革的绝对多数，”Eisenkot在投票前表示。
投票发生在10月27日议会选举数周之后，那次选举中内塔尼亚胡及其盟友失去了议会多数。随后，以色列总统责成Eisenkot尝试组建新的联合政府。
Eisenkot最多还有五周时间，以争取足够盟友组建联合政府。
在场外谈判继续进行的同时，他的阵营以及无所属的阿拉伯主导政党，可以利用他们在新宣誓就职的以色列议会中的多数，推进立法议程。
他们上周提交了若干法案，包括为总理职务设定任期限制、就哈马斯主导的2023年10月7日袭击成立政府主导的调查，以及撤销限制司法权的法律。
据耶路撒冷智库Israel Democracy Institute的Assaf Shapira称，Kahana的任职给反对派阵营带来重大立法优势。
“这一点很重要，因为时间不多了，以色列议会议长可以让立法进程快得多，也可以慢得多，”Shapira说。
Kahana接替内塔尼亚胡盟友Amir Ohana担任议长。

blocks.alt: Gadi Eisenkot speaks at microphones, with Israeli flags behind him at the Knesset

blocks.text: Gadi Eisenkot受命尝试组建新的以色列政府。照片：Abir Sultan/EPA

Shapira说，即便内塔尼亚胡的反对者仍将拥有多数，他们也会“觉得势头已过”，并且“部分立法将被推迟，这是实实在在的危险”。
议事程序将构成进一步的挑战。一项法案必须在全院提出，经委员会审议，并在全院多次表决后才能在克奈塞特通过。这一曲折过程可能使法案难以在时限到来前走完全程。
沙皮拉说，艾森科特及其盟友可能会优先推动废止那些让政府在法官任命中拥有更大权力、并削弱以色列总检察长权力的争议性法律；总检察长是一个独立职位，被许多人视为以色列政府制衡体系的核心。
“废除这些法律非常容易，因为不必设立新的机构，”他说。
Shapira还说，一旦政府组成，设立机构调查10月7日袭击会更容易，也更具合法性。
内塔尼亚胡的反对者认为，他阻止了对那一天——以色列历史上伤亡最惨重的一天——任何军事或情报失误进行独立调查，并逃避了问责。

items.title: Caribbean nations fear economic impact of shuttering citizenship program after EU threats
items.summary: St Kitts and Nevis to wind down citizenship-by-investment program after EU warns of end to visa-free access The decision by St Kitts and Nevis to end a lucrative programme offering citizenship to wealthy foreigners in exchange for investment threatens its economy and ability to support people in nee…
items.body:
St Kitts and Nevis’s prime minister, Terrance Drew, addresses the UN general assembly in New York City on 23 September 2023. Photograph: Eduardo Muñoz/Reuters

St Kitts and Nevis’s prime minister, Terrance Drew, addresses the UN general assembly in New York City on 23 September 2023. Photograph: Eduardo Muñoz/Reuters

Caribbean nations fear economic impact of shuttering citizenship program after EU threats

St Kitts and Nevis to wind down citizenship-by-investment program after EU warns of end to visa-free access

The decision by St Kitts and Nevis to end a lucrative programme offering citizenship to wealthy foreigners in exchange for investment threatens its economy and ability to support people in need, the premier of the island of Nevis has warned.

On Friday, Terrance Drew, the prime minister of the twin-island Caribbean nation, announced he would wind down the citizenship-by-investment (CBI) programme, after the European Union threatened to end visa-free access for St Kitts and Nevis.

Mark Brantley, the premier of Nevis, which has autonomous self-governance in some aspects, said he understood that the “country was given very little choice”, but did not “support the winding down of the program”.

The 42-year-old CBI programme, which St Kitts and Nevis pioneered, allows wealthy foreigners to obtain citizenship and ultimately a passport by investing in infrastructure and other development projects. It has brought billions of dollars into the country and in some years accounted for the largest share of government revenue.

In June, the European Commission wrote to the five Caribbean nations that currently operate CBI programmes: St Kitts and Nevis, Dominica, Antigua and Barbuda, Grenada and St Lucia. It warned that countries may lose visa-free access to its 29-country Schengen area if they did not phase out CBI.

In Friday’s statement, Drew blamed concerns over the programme on mismanagement by previous administrations, including years of underselling to undercut other countries, a controversial prison project, weak escrow protections and investment sums not being properly paid into the citizenship unit.

He said his government had led major reforms to the Caribbean’s programmes with international partners, including the US treasury, but argued that continuing the programme risked visa-free travel to parts of Europe and access to international banking. That could disrupt services allowing visitors to use overseas cards and families abroad to send money home.

Brantley, however, argued it was unfair for the EU to force St Kitts and Nevis to make a move without offering assistance to navigate the transition to other industries.

“I have not yet seen from the EU any corresponding suggestions of assistance. And we have to realise that these citizenship-by-investment programs, not only in St Kitts and Nevis, but … smaller countries of the Caribbean, have contributed significantly to our gross domestic product and also to ensuring that our people … can get adequate access to water and to education, to healthcare and the like,” he said.

Brantley described the 1 June 2028 deadline the EU gave the country to phase out the lucrative programme as “frankly ludicrous”.

In his statement, Drew said the CBI programme “did a lot of good, but it also created a danger”.

“When one source pays for half or more of everything, you are at its mercy. If it stops, everything stops. That is putting all of your eggs in one basket,” he added.

The prime minister said the government aimed to diversify its economy by strengthening tourism, yachting, and digital and creative industries, among others. He added that the sale of clean, geothermal energy was “at the heart of it” with drilling and exploration already planned.

“I will not pretend that the road is easy. Less CBI money means we must spend wisely and plan carefully. We will. Our plan is to make this change by growing our economy. Raising taxes is not part of that plan,” Drew said.

Antigua and Barbuda has also expressed willingness to end the programme, though it is trying to negotiate a longer transition period. The five Caribbean governments have taken differing positions on the EU demand. According to local media, Grenada has indicated it wants its programme to continue until 2032, while Dominica and St Lucia have responded to Brussels without publicly committing to ending their programmes.

Jermine Abel in Basseterre contributed reporting

items.summary: Indigenous Awá people of Amazon make contact with villagers and accept food to take back to territory About 20 Indigenous people emerged from isolation in Brazil’s Amazon rainforest, several organizations reported on Tuesday, raising the alarm about increased invasions into the tribe’s territory. Ac…
items.body:
People identified as members of the Awá Indigenous group appear in the Arariboia Indigenous Territory, Maranhão state, Brazil. Photograph: Guajajara Community/Survival International/Reuters

People identified as members of the Awá Indigenous group appear in the Arariboia Indigenous Territory, Maranhão state, Brazil. Photograph: Guajajara Community/Survival International/Reuters

Isolated Brazilian tribe emerges amid alarm over threats to group’s way of life

Indigenous Awá people of Amazon make contact with villagers and accept food to take back to territory

About 20 Indigenous people emerged from isolation in Brazil’s Amazon rainforest, several organizations reported on Tuesday, raising the alarm about increased invasions into the tribe’s territory.

According to the NGO Survival International, members of the Awá people, who live in voluntary isolation, arrived on Monday in a village and made contact with a government team in a “historic encounter”.

The village they entered was within the Arariboia Indigenous territory in the north-eastern state of Maranhão, home to the Guajajara ethnic group.

Local community leaders said the villagers offered food to the group.

“They asked for yams and took them back into their forest,” said Survival International.

A group of young Awá men in the north-eastern state of Maranhão in 2017. Photograph: Scott Wallace/Getty Images

The NGO explained that the Awá typically subsist on hunting and gathering. However, they have faced increased incursions from illegal loggers, hunters and cattle ranchers.

A video of the encounter, filmed by Guajajara villagers and released by Survival International, shows a group of men, women and children at the edge of the forest.

Partially concealed by vegetation, they appear naked and are wearing necklaces. The men carry bows and long arrows.

“The physical condition of some members, particularly the children and the elderly, caused concern among the villagers, who noted clear signs of severe emaciation,” warned Coapima, an organization representing Indigenous groups in Maranhão.

Coapima highlighted the risks that unplanned contact poses to such groups, noting that they are particularly “exposed to diseases” against which they have little to no immunity.

Funai, the public agency responsible for Indigenous affairs, said in a statement sent to AFP that its technical teams were closely monitoring the situation and analyzing available information regarding the group’s health.

巴西与世隔绝的部落现身，外界对其生活方式受到威胁深感担忧
亚马孙阿瓦原住民与村民接触，并接受食物带回领地
若干组织周二报告，约20名原住民从巴西亚马孙雨林的隔绝状态中走出，并警告对该部落领地的入侵正在增加。
据非政府组织Survival International称，选择自愿隔绝生活的阿瓦人成员周一来到一座村庄，并与一个政府团队接触，这是一次“历史性相遇”。
他们进入的村庄位于东北部马拉尼昂州的阿拉里博亚原住民领地内，那里是瓜贾哈拉族的家园。
当地社区领袖说，村民向这群人提供了食物。
“他们要了山药，然后带回森林里，”Survival International说。

blocks.alt: Portrait of a group of young Awa men as they pose with their hunting bows and arrows

blocks.text: 2017年，巴西东北部马拉尼昂州的一群阿瓦青年男子。照片：Scott Wallace/Getty Images
该非政府组织解释说，阿瓦人通常以狩猎和采集为生。然而，他们面临来自非法伐木者、猎人和牧牛场主越来越多的入侵。
这段由瓜贾哈拉村民拍摄、经Survival International发布的接触视频，显示一群男女和儿童站在森林边缘。
他们部分被植被遮挡，看起来未着衣物，戴着项链。这些男子带着弓和长箭。
“一些成员的身体状况，尤其是儿童和老人，引起了村民的担忧，他们注意到明显的严重消瘦迹象，”代表马拉尼昂州原住民群体的组织Coapima警告说。
Coapima强调了计划外接触给此类群体带来的风险，指出他们尤其“容易感染疾病”，而他们对此几乎没有免疫力。
负责原住民事务的公共机构Funai在发给法新社的声明中表示，其技术团队正在密切监测局势，并分析有关该群体健康状况的现有信息。
Survival International的负责人Caroline Pearce说，该群体选择走出隔绝状态，是一个“令人不安的信号，说明对未接触族群森林的持续侵入，正在把原本可以自给自足的原住民置于真正的危险之中”。
她说，阿瓦人正被逼入“亚马孙雨林中一块越来越小、四周都是毁坏的孤岛”。

据Survival International称，许多守护者在试图保护他们与阿瓦人共享的领地时失去了生命。

items.title: Eight-year-old Haitian boy returns home after release from ICE custody
items.summary: Child reunited with family after he was detained by immigration agents in San Diego and transferred to Texas An eight-year-old Haitian boy who was put into restraints and detained by immigration agents in San Diego on 4 November and transferred to a facility in Texas has been reunited with his famil…
items.body:
An eight-year-old boy is welcomed home after being released from ICE custody in a post on X by Representative Juan Vargas. Photograph: Rep Juan Vargas via X

An eight-year-old boy is welcomed home after being released from ICE custody in a post on X by Representative Juan Vargas. Photograph: Rep Juan Vargas via X

Eight-year-old Haitian boy returns home after release from ICE custody

Child reunited with family after he was detained by immigration agents in San Diego and transferred to Texas

An eight-year-old Haitian boy who was put into restraints and detained by immigration agents in San Diego on 4 November and transferred to a facility in Texas has been reunited with his family in California.

Representative Juan Vargas shared a photograph of the boy and his family in a social media post on Monda, writing: “11 days ago, an 8-year-old in San Diego was taken into federal custody during an immigration check-in. He was separated from his loved ones and held in a facility in Texas. Today, he’s finally home.”

The Haitian Bridge Alliance, an immigration advocacy group, confirmed that the third-grader had been released from Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) custody.

“An eight-year-old child belongs in a classroom, on a playground, and surrounded by love – not in immigration detention. We welcome his release, but his freedom should never have required a public outcry,” Guerline Jozef, executive director of the Haitian Bridge Alliance, said in a statement.

Hundreds protest against ex-border patrol chief Greg Bovino at Rutgers University talk

Read more

The third-grader at Fay elementary school was put in restraints and taken into custody by federal immigration officers at a check-in earlier in the month, according to video obtained by NBC News and an oversight letter Democratic lawmakers sent to the Departments of Homeland Security and Health and Human Services.

A spokesperson for the homeland security department said ICE took the child into custody “out of an abundance of caution and to ensure the child’s safety”.

The uncle, the spokesperson said in a statement to the Guardian, was unable to prove legal guardianship – and that officials were obliged by federal anti-trafficking laws to take the boy into care as an “unaccompanied alien child”.

The Haitian Bridge Alliance said the boy was in the care of his uncle and cousins after his father was deported last year.

“I’m so grateful that he’s home, but this should have never happened in the first place,” Vargas said in a second social media post, adding that he would be asking the Trump administration for answers. While he was detained, the child was “held in a facility in Texas, far away from his home in San Diego”, Vargas said.

Celebrating the boy’s return, Jozef of the Haitian Bridge Alliance told NBC News: “The aunt was literally crying, and she said: ‘I have not eaten since the Wednesday they took my baby.’ They haven’t been able to sleep because of that.” She added: “The cousins were there when they took him, and wondering: will they ever see him again? But today [Monday] they are able to see him again. They are able to hug him.”

items.title: Five EU states announce plans for immigration ‘return hubs’ in Rwanda
items.summary: Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’ Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face leg…
items.body:
The Danish PM, Mette Frederiksen (centre), Austrian chancellor Christian Stocker (second left), and Rwandan minister Vincent Biruta (right) in Vienna on Monday. Photograph: Leonhard Föger/Reuters

The Danish PM, Mette Frederiksen (centre), Austrian chancellor Christian Stocker (second left), and Rwandan minister Vincent Biruta (right) in Vienna on Monday. Photograph: Leonhard Föger/Reuters

Five EU states announce plans for immigration ‘return hubs’ in Rwanda

Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’

Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”.

The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s newly agreed returns law that allows people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe to be sent to a third country.

In a statement released on Monday the five EU countries said “concrete negotiations with partner country Rwanda will begin for implementation”, saying the scheme would make “an important contribution to further curbing illegal migration, dismantling the business model of smugglers and relieving the burden on our population”.

Officials hope to send 100 people to Rwanda from early next year to test the model. The scheme will apply to adults whose claims to asylum have been rejected or others with no legal right to live in the EU.

In theory, according to diplomatic sources, migrants would stay in a reception centre in Rwanda for a couple of months, before choosing to integrate into life in the Great Lakes country or return to their home nation.

Unlike the failed scheme pursued by the British Conservative government in Rwanda, or Italy’s agreement with Albania, it will not apply to people pursuing asylum claims.

The reception centre, which would be an open facility, was not intended to house people long term but to accommodate regular flows of people, the countries said. Diplomatic sources said the EU countries were not using British-funded facilities built in Kigali.

Hope Hostel in Kigali was prepared to house asylum seekers sent from Britain to Rwanda under the Conservatives’ prepared scheme. Photograph: AP

The governments involved argue it will protect the European asylum system while removing the incentive for irregular migrants to come to Europe.

Denmark’s immigration minister, Morten Bødskov, whose government has pioneered a tough line on migration widely emulated across the EU, said it was “a huge breakthrough”.

The German interior minister, Alexander Dobrindt, said: “Return hubs offer a positive approach for people without the right to stay and with no prospects in Europe, whose countries of origin do not cooperate in the repatriation process.”

Andy Burnham told reporters last week that the UK had not had direct discussions with European governments involved in return hubs but “we will watch that with interest, learning from what went on in the past. The public want us to do whatever we can to deal with illegal immigration.”

Critics have highlighted the ethical difficulties of striking an agreement with Rwanda’s repressive government, which was found in 2024 by the US state department to allow state security forces and civilian officials to commit human rights abuses with impunity, while also raising concerns about freedom of expression and forced labour.

The French Green MEP Mélissa Camara denounced the agreement between the five countries and Rwanda as “an agreement of shame” and “a grave moral failing”. She said: “Under this agreement, people will be deported thousands of kilometres away from the European Union, with no guarantees regarding the compliance with their rights.”

Alain Berset, the secretary general of the Council of Europe, the continent’s human rights body, said it was not possible “to be so precise a priori” about what any return hubs proposal meant. Speaking to the Guardian before the announcement, he said all members of the Council of Europe were committed to the European convention on human rights “and this must be the lighthouse” for all discussions on return hubs.

“On concrete cases, then we will have to see if this is compliant with the convention,” he said. He stressed that “all countries must be able to define their migration policy”.

Officials involved in setting up the migration centres expect legal challenges, but say the scheme is grounded in human rights law.

Rights organisations say the scheme is bound to fail. “Member states may call them ‘return hubs’ or even ‘welcome centres’, but no euphemism can hide the violence of uprooting people from the life they’ve been building in Europe, and sending them to a country they don’t even know, without family, networks or meaningful prospects,” said Chiara Catelli of Picum, a pan-European organisation that campaigns for the rights of undocumented migrants.

丹麦首相梅特·弗雷泽里克森（中）、奥地利总理克里斯蒂安·施托克尔（左二）和卢旺达部长文森特·比鲁塔（右）周一在维也纳。摄影：Leonhard Föger/路透社

丹麦首相梅特·弗雷泽里克森（中）、奥地利总理克里斯蒂安·施托克尔（左二）和卢旺达部长文森特·比鲁塔（右）周一在维也纳。摄影：Leonhard Föger/路透社

五个欧盟国家宣布计划在卢旺达设立移民“遣返中心”

德国、奥地利、荷兰、丹麦和希腊可能面临对该政策的挑战，该政策被批评为“严重的道德失范”

五个欧盟成员国宣布计划在卢旺达设立一个离岸中心，用于安置无权留在欧洲的人。这一试点计划预计将面临法律挑战，并已被谴责为“严重的道德失范”。

这五个国家——德国、奥地利、荷兰、丹麦和希腊——是首批寻求利用欧盟新近达成的遣返法的国家。该法律允许将已用尽所有针对被逐出欧洲的上诉途径的人送往第三国。

这五个欧盟国家在周一发布的一份声明中表示，“将与伙伴国卢旺达开始具体谈判以实施”该计划，并称该计划将“为进一步遏制非法移民、瓦解走私者的商业模式以及减轻我们民众的负担作出重要贡献”。

官员们希望从明年初起将100人送往卢旺达以测试该模式。该计划将适用于庇护申请被拒的成年人或其他无权在欧盟居住的人。

据外交消息人士称，理论上，移民将在卢旺达的一个接待中心停留几个月，然后选择融入这个大湖地区国家的生活或返回自己的祖国。

与英国保守党政府在卢旺达推行但已失败的计划，或意大利与阿尔巴尼亚的协议不同，该计划不适用于正在申请庇护的人。

这些国家表示，该接待中心将是一个开放式设施，并非用于长期安置人员，而是用于接待定期流动的人员。外交消息人士称，这些欧盟国家不会使用英国在基加利出资建造的设施。

根据保守党政府拟定的计划，基加利的希望旅舍曾被准备用于安置从英国送往卢旺达的寻求庇护者。摄影：美联社

参与其中的各国政府主张，该计划将保护欧洲庇护体系，同时消除非正规移民前往欧洲的动机。

丹麦移民大臣莫滕·博兹科夫表示，这是“一个巨大的突破”。其政府在移民问题上率先采取强硬路线，并在欧盟范围内被广泛效仿。

德国内政部长亚历山大·多布林特表示：“遣返中心为那些无权居留、在欧洲没有前景、且原籍国在遣返过程中不予合作的人提供了一种积极的处理方式。”

安迪·伯纳姆上周告诉记者，英国尚未与参与遣返中心的欧洲各国政府进行直接讨论，但“我们将饶有兴趣地关注此事，并从过去的经验中学习。公众希望我们尽一切努力处理非法移民问题。”

批评者强调了与卢旺达压制性政府达成协议的道德难题。美国国务院在2024年认定卢旺达允许国家安全部队和文职官员肆意侵犯人权而不受惩罚，同时还对言论自由和强迫劳动提出关切。

法国绿党欧洲议会议员梅利莎·卡马拉谴责五国与卢旺达之间的协议是“一项可耻的协议”和“严重的道德失范”。她说：“根据这项协议，人们将被驱逐到距离欧盟数千公里之外的地方，而其权利是否得到遵守没有任何保障。”

欧洲人权机构欧洲委员会秘书长阿兰·贝尔塞表示，无法“事先就如此精确地”判断任何遣返中心提案意味着什么。在宣布之前接受《卫报》采访时，他表示欧洲委员会所有成员都致力于遵守《欧洲人权公约》，“这必须成为”所有关于遣返中心讨论的“灯塔”。

“至于具体案例，我们届时将不得不看这是否符合公约，”他说。他强调“所有国家都必须能够界定自己的移民政策”。

参与设立移民中心的官员预计会面临法律挑战，但表示该计划以人权法为依据。

人权组织表示该计划注定失败。“成员国可以称它们为‘遣返中心’甚至‘欢迎中心’，但任何委婉说法都无法掩盖将人们从他们在欧洲建立的生活中连根拔起，并将他们送往一个他们甚至不认识、没有家人、没有社会网络、也没有有意义前景的国家的暴力，”为无证移民权利奔走的泛欧组织Picum的基娅拉·卡泰利说。

items.body:
‘When the sun came out it felt like it opened a scar’ – This is climate breakdown

When the floods hit Pakistan he went out to help. Then the water reached his own family. This is Imran Lodhi’s story

• Location: Dera Ghazi Khan, Pakistan

• Disaster: Pakistan intense monsoon rainfall

Imran Lodhi is a university lecturer with a doctorate in climate change and sustainable development. The 41-year-old was living in Dera Ghazi Khan, a city in south-western Punjab, when floods devastated provinces across Pakistan. Climate change made the monsoon rainfall that caused the floods more intense.

In 2022, I was living in an area that had less risk of flooding. I had a small child and my PhD thesis was just a few weeks away. I tried to avoid flood news on social media until I saw a picture of a two-year-old girl who was buried in mud. It was probably her last breath. She died after that. That was the turning point.

Imran Lodhi immediately rallied friends to help victims of the devastating flooding across Pakistan in 2022. Photograph: Zoral Naik

I immediately called my friends, six to seven people, in a mosque. I talked to them: “We don’t know what to do, but at least we can start from somewhere.” Initially, it was food. We hired some commercial cooks.

We planned to work only in villages close to our city. A lot of people were taking refuge in nearby high places, high enough that the water did not reach them. On the first day we went with some food to the nearest village.

When the rain is over, the sun comes out. Usually, it’s a good sign. But, in those areas, it didn’t feel good. It felt like it opened a scar. The pain that was hiding somehow had become open. It was like being naked. I could see trolleys, tractors, vehicles and homes all drowned in the flood. There was nothing from the government, nothing from any development sector. There was no camp. People were just living under open skies.

Men felt that their women being in an open place was a kind of emotional damage for them. It was not normal for most of the people here. Many women never came out. They came out for their work, the agriculture work, but not sitting that openly among the public. Their hair was full of dust and dry mud. Their clothes had a heavy layer of dry mud; no shoes on their feet. Mothers were not breastfeeding. Babies crying for milk, and the milk was not there. Mothers trying to soothe them with fake sounds.

The cows did not have feed and were not giving milk. Many of the animals were lost, their bodies wide open, decomposed. Then the water, which stayed there for a week, started to smell very bad. There was no good smell.

Families displaced by flooding in Balochistan province were forced to live in tents on causeways and other higher ground. Photograph: Fida Hussain/AFP/Getty Images

We prepared food in the morning. Then we prepared food at lunchtime. We generally finished distributing food around 8pm. One night it was 11pm and we thought some people might not have food. So we just cooked some food late at night and went to every camp.

One old woman started to laugh. I was surprised. I asked her: “It’s OK, we have food, but why are you laughing?” And she said: “I was just complaining, ‘Lord, that you left me with an empty stomach today.’ And suddenly you appeared.”

It was a very strange experience for her. For us also. People, when they are in tough conditions, are attached to their beliefs. And, when things like that come up, they establish a spiritual connection with the people who are helping out.

Flooding in the historic city of Sehwan in September 2022. The climate crisis made monsoon rainfall more intense. Photograph: Akhtar Soomro/Reuters

We posted on social media. We tried to mobilise. A lot of people contacted us who were from other parts of Pakistan. Money poured in and we kept expanding the team. From two or three villages, we started to cover the entire district, and then almost the entire region.

The government protocols were to not go into certain areas that looked dangerous or were not safe for a boat. Families were trapped, many, many kilometres into the water. There was no land in one village. Small wooden cupboards were hung on trees so stuff could be saved from the water. The immediate shelter was a big tree near them. The whole family was in the tree. The elders were lying on the branches. They somehow made a swing for the kids. They spent days in those trees.

A few villages were completely destroyed. Not a single home was standing. Everything was in shock, even the trees. One old woman who was living with her married kids was not ready to leave that rubble. She was so attached to that home that she felt like there was no life after it. She had a small cupboard in which she kept some small things to sell, for her independence. She was so concerned about that small cupboard. When I reached there, that cupboard was all broken.

People use a raft to navigate a flooded district of Hyderabad, Pakistan, in August 2022. Photograph: Akram Shahid/AFP/Getty Images

One day I had a fever and my wife stopped me: “Don’t go out – you are not well enough to help other people.” But I still went out to a village to help people. When we reached there, I got news that the city we were living in – which I thought was safe – suddenly was a source of threat. There was water coming toward the city. Within hours, the water would be in the city. My family was there. And I was almost 100km away.

So I rushed back. But the road toward the city was cut off by the flood. There was no way I could go back to my family. I called my wife and I asked them to stay vigilant and look out for water in the city. I gave them some suggestions: how they could save themselves and evacuate. That was a very, very tough call.

Children take refuge in the grounds of a school after flooding in Jacobabad. Exceptional monsoon rainfall from June to October 2022 killed more than 1,700 people in Pakistan. Photograph: Akhtar Soomro/Reuters

Eventually, the city was saved. Next day, we took a boat to get past the road that was cut off. Sitting in that boat, I was thinking about my family. Once I reached the other side, I called some people to take me home.

When I reached home, I had a very strong fever and I spent that day at home. I tried to behave normally, but everybody knew I was not feeling well. I took one day off from community work.

The next day I wanted to stop. But the problem was, I was in the middle of that network. If I stop, this whole process will stop. This whole network of relief work will stop.

The next day, even with a high fever, I left for the field because I didn’t want that to stop. When I grew up, the community fabric was very strong. It was common practice that whenever people got sick, got in an accident, hospitalised, people would visit the person and share some money.

Rescue workers use a boat to transport children after flooding in Dera Ghazi Khan, Punjab province, in August 2022. Photograph: Shahid Saeed Mirza/AFP/Getty Images

This was the kind of culture I observed happening around me.

I went back to those areas where the flood came. There was still some water standing so there were remains of that devastation. But there’s a very common sweet in that area we call jalebi. I can smell that sweet in those villages. I see shops open. I see farmers, labourers. I felt good watching people working again. It looked like life was coming back.

There was an annual poetry event happening three months after the flood. Saraiki culture is very rich, one of the oldest. I was consulted by one of my friends who is the organiser of that event. Should we suspend this year’s events or not?

I said you should never suspend the event. Let people believe the normalisation, let people believe in the spirit of survival. They organised the poetry event.

One day I had a fever and my wife stopped me: “Don’t go out – you are not well enough to help other people.” But I still went out to a village to help people. When we reached there, I got news that the city we were living in – which I thought was safe – suddenly was a source of threat. There was water coming toward the city. Within hours, the water would be in the city. My family was there. And I was almost 100km away.

So I rushed back. But the road toward the city was cut off by the flood. There was no way I could go back to my family. I called my wife and I asked them to stay vigilant and look out for water in the city. I gave them some suggestions: how they could save themselves and evacuate. That was a very, very tough call.

blocks.text: Children take refuge in the grounds of a school after flooding in Jacobabad. Exceptional monsoon rainfall from June to October 2022 killed more than 1,700 people in Pakistan. Photograph: Akhtar Soomro/Reuters

Eventually, the city was saved. Next day, we took a boat to get past the road that was cut off. Sitting in that boat, I was thinking about my family. Once I reached the other side, I called some people to take me home.
When I reached home, I had a very strong fever and I spent that day at home. I tried to behave normally, but everybody knew I was not feeling well. I took one day off from community work.
The next day I wanted to stop. But the problem was, I was in the middle of that network. If I stop, this whole process will stop. This whole network of relief work will stop.

The next day, even with a high fever, I left for the field because I didn’t want that to stop. When I grew up, the community fabric was very strong. It was common practice that whenever people got sick, got in an accident, hospitalised, people would visit the person and share some money.

This was the kind of culture I observed happening around me.

I went back to those areas where the flood came. There was still some water standing so there were remains of that devastation. But there’s a very common sweet in that area we call jalebi. I can smell that sweet in those villages. I see shops open. I see farmers, labourers. I felt good watching people working again. It looked like life was coming back.

There was an annual poetry event happening three months after the flood. Saraiki culture is very rich, one of the oldest. I was consulted by one of my friends who is the organiser of that event. Should we suspend this year’s events or not?
I said you should never suspend the event. Let people believe the normalisation, let people believe in the spirit of survival. They organised the poetry event.

“当太阳出来时，感觉像揭开了一道伤疤”——这是气候崩溃

当洪水袭击巴基斯坦时，他外出帮忙。然后洪水波及了他自己的家人。这是伊姆兰·洛迪的故事

• 地点：巴基斯坦德拉加齐汗

• 灾害：巴基斯坦强季风降雨

伊姆兰·洛迪是一位拥有气候变化与可持续发展博士学位的大学讲师。41岁的他住在旁遮普省西南部的德拉加齐汗市，当时洪水摧毁了巴基斯坦多个省份。气候变化使导致洪水的季风降雨更加强烈。

2022年，我住在一个洪水风险较低的地区。我有一个年幼的孩子，我的博士论文还有几周就要完成了。我试图避开社交媒体上的洪水新闻，直到我看到一张两岁女孩被埋在泥里的照片。那可能是她最后一口气。她在那之后去世了。那是转折点。

伊姆兰·洛迪立即召集朋友帮助2022年巴基斯坦毁灭性洪水的受害者。照片：佐拉尔·奈克

我立刻在一座清真寺里打电话给我的朋友，六七个人。我对他们说：“我们不知道该做什么，但至少可以从某个地方开始。”起初是食物。我们雇了一些商业厨师。

我们计划只在我们城市附近的村庄工作。很多人正在附近的高处避难，高到水淹不到他们。第一天我们带着一些食物去了最近的村庄。

雨停后，太阳出来了。通常，这是个好兆头。但在那些地区，感觉并不好。感觉像揭开了一道伤疤。隐藏的痛苦不知怎地暴露了出来。就像赤身裸体一样。我看到手推车、拖拉机、车辆和房屋全都淹没在洪水中。政府没有任何援助，任何发展部门也没有。没有营地。人们就住在露天之下。

男人们觉得他们的女人待在露天场所对他们来说是一种情感伤害。这对这里的大多数人来说是不正常的。许多女人从未出来过。她们出来是为了干活，干农活，但不是那样公开地坐在公众中间。她们的头发满是灰尘和干泥。她们的衣服上有一层厚厚的干泥；脚上没有鞋子。母亲们没有在哺乳。婴儿哭着要奶，而奶水没有。母亲们试图用假声音安抚他们。

奶牛没有饲料，也不产奶。许多动物失踪了，它们的尸体敞开着，已经腐烂。然后，在那里停留了一周的水开始散发出非常难闻的气味。没有好闻的气味。

俾路支省因洪水而流离失所的家庭被迫住在堤道和其他高地上的帐篷里。照片：菲达·侯赛因/法新社/盖蒂图片社

我们早上准备食物。然后午餐时间准备食物。我们通常在晚上8点左右完成食物分发。有一天晚上到了11点，我们想有些人可能没有食物。所以我们深夜做了些食物，去了每个营地。

一位老妇人开始笑起来。我很惊讶。我问她：“没事，我们有食物，但你为什么笑？”她说：“我刚才还在抱怨，‘主啊，你今天让我空着肚子。’然后你突然出现了。”

这对她来说是一次非常奇怪的经历。对我们也是。人们在艰难处境中会依附于他们的信仰。而当这样的事情出现时，他们会与提供帮助的人建立一种精神联系。

2022年9月历史名城塞赫万发生洪水。气候危机使季风降雨更加强烈。照片：阿赫塔尔·苏姆罗/路透社

我们在社交媒体上发帖。我们试图动员起来。许多来自巴基斯坦其他地方的人联系我们。钱涌了进来，我们不断扩充团队。从两三个村庄开始，我们覆盖了整个地区，然后几乎整个区域。

政府的规程是不进入某些看起来危险或对船只不安全的地区。家庭被困在洪水深处许多公里处。一个村庄没有陆地。小木柜挂在树上，以便东西能从水中保存下来。眼前的避难所是他们附近的一棵大树。全家人都在树上。老人们躺在树枝上。他们设法为孩子们做了一个秋千。他们在那些树上待了好几天。

几个村庄被完全摧毁。没有一座房屋立着。一切都在震惊中，甚至树木也是。一位与已婚子女同住的老妇人不愿离开那片废墟。她对那个家如此依恋，以至于她觉得那之后没有生活了。她有一个小柜子，里面放着一些要卖的小东西，为了她的独立。她如此在意那个小柜子。当我到达那里时，那个柜子全坏了。

2022年8月，人们用木筏在巴基斯坦海得拉巴被洪水淹没的地区航行。照片：阿克拉姆·沙希德/法新社/盖蒂图片社

有一天我发烧了，我妻子拦住我：“别出去——你身体不够好，帮不了别人。”但我还是出去到一个村庄帮助人们。当我们到达那里时，我得到消息说我们居住的城市——我以为安全的城市——突然成了威胁的来源。有水正朝城市涌来。几个小时内，水就会进入城市。我的家人就在那里。而我离那里将近100公里。

所以我赶了回去。但通往城市的道路被洪水切断了。我无法回到家人身边。我打电话给妻子，让他们保持警惕，注意城里的水。我给了他们一些建议：如何自救和撤离。那是一个非常非常艰难的决定。

雅各布阿巴德洪水后，孩子们在学校操场上避难。2022年6月至10月的异常季风降雨在巴基斯坦造成1700多人死亡。照片：阿赫塔尔·苏姆罗/路透社

最终，城市得救了。第二天，我们乘船绕过被切断的道路。坐在那条船上，我想着我的家人。一到对岸，我就打电话叫人带我回家。

到家时，我发着高烧，那天我待在家里。我试图表现得正常，但每个人都知道我不舒服。我从社区工作中休息了一天。

第二天我想停下来。但问题是，我处在那张网络的中心。如果我停下来，整个进程就会停止。整个救援工作网络就会停止。

第二天，即使发着高烧，我还是去了现场，因为我不想让那停下来。在我成长过程中，社区结构非常牢固。每当人们生病、出事故、住院时，人们会去看望那个人并分享一些钱，这是常见的做法。

2022年8月，旁遮普省德拉加齐汗洪水后，救援人员用船运送儿童。照片：沙希德·赛义德·米尔扎/法新社/盖蒂图片社

这就是我在周围观察到的文化。

我回到了洪水来袭的那些地区。还有一些水积在那里，所以有那场毁灭的痕迹。但那个地区有一种很常见的甜食，我们叫它贾莱比。我能在那些村庄闻到那种甜食的味道。我看到商店开门。我看到农民、劳工。看到人们再次工作，我感觉很好。看起来生活正在回来。

洪水过后三个月，有一场年度诗歌活动。萨拉基文化非常丰富，是最古老的文化之一。我的一位朋友是那个活动的组织者，他咨询了我。我们今年应该暂停活动还是不暂停？

我说你永远不应该暂停活动。让人们相信正常化，让人们相信生存的精神。他们组织了诗歌活动。
